7	    /// `export` — ⌘E (`EditorViewController.exportProjectCommand` and
8	    /// `ExportSheetController`). The preset names the ENCODING — a container
9	    /// and a codec, nothing about size — and the size is the sheet's separate
10	    /// choice, in the Size popup's own vocabulary and defaulting as the popup
11	    /// does to its first row: the document's size, or an image format's cap.
12	    /// The CORE resolves both into concrete settings (`rc_export_settings`)
13	    /// that go to the same `Exporter.export` the sheet uses: there is exactly
14	    /// one writer, so an agent export and a menu export cannot disagree.
15	    ///
16	    /// Answers AT ONCE (spec §11 #326): every refusal is made here, before
17	    /// anything is queued — the arguments, the core's settings, the folder
18	    /// and the graphics gate — and the export is then a job in the Export
19	    /// Queue, exactly as the sheet's Add to Queue makes one, answered as
20	    /// `{export_id, path, status}`. `export_status` follows the job and
21	    /// `cancel_export` stops it (`AgentServer+ExportStatus.swift`); a failure
22	    /// while writing comes back from there. The queue window is not shown.
23	    ///
24	    /// One argument is NOT a setting and never reaches the core:
25	    /// `burn_in_timecode` is a recipe option (`RecipeOptions`), read below
26	    /// beside the overrides it deliberately does not join.
27	    ///
28	    /// The finished job's answer carries the sound the file actually holds —
29	    /// its integrated loudness and true peak, measured on the way through —
30	    /// for every format that has any, whether `loudness_lufs` was asked for
31	    /// or not, and, with `stems` (the sheet's Stems popup, spec §11 AU-108),
32	    /// each stem file beside the mix.
33	    func exportProject(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
34	        // The clock `export_status`'s `elapsed` runs on, read before any check.
35	        let started = ProcessInfo.processInfo.systemUptime
36	        let presetID = try requiredString(a, "preset")
37	        let path = try requiredString(a, "path")
38	        let wholeProject = (try stringArg(a, "range") ?? "project").lowercased()
39	        guard ["project", "in_out"].contains(wholeProject) else {
40	            throw ToolError(
41	                message: "range must be \"project\" (the whole timeline) or \"in_out\" "
42	                    + "(the in/out range set_range set), not \"\(wholeProject)\".")
43	        }
44	        // The export sheet's burn-in checkbox — and read HERE rather than
45	        // into `overrides` below, which is the whole of the decision. A
46	        // recipe option changes the PICTURE, so it travels with the
47	        // description of the picture: `export_overrides.rs` ignores a key it
48	        // does not know, on purpose, so a `burn_in_timecode` posted through
49	        // `rc_export_settings` would vanish without a word and this tool
50	        // would report success on an un-burnt file. It goes to `Exporter`
51	        // beside the settings instead (`RecipeOptions`, `Exporter.export`),
52	        // which is also what reaches GIF and APNG — those never go through
53	        // `ExportWriter` at all.
54	        let options = RecipeOptions(burnInTimecode: try boolArg(a, "burn_in_timecode") ?? false)
55	        let prepared = try onMain {
56	            () throws -> (ProjectDocument, ReelProject, [UInt32: URL], ExportSettings, GraphicSet?)
57	            in
58	            let document = try self.target(a)
59	            guard document.project.duration > 0 else {
60	                throw ToolError(message: "There is nothing on the timeline to export.")
61	            }
62	            // The Range popup of the export sheet, in the sheet's own terms:
63	            // "Whole project" is no override at all, "In/out range" is the
64	            // core's ONE nested `range` object (`export.rs`). The core snaps
65	            // it to the frame grid and clamps it to the project.
66	            var overrides: [String: Any] = [:]
67	            if wholeProject == "in_out" {
68	                guard let range = document.inOutRange, range.end > range.start else {
69	                    throw ToolError(
70	                        message: "This project has no in/out range — set one with set_range "
71	                            + "{start, end}, or export with range \"project\".")
72	                }
73	                overrides["range"] = ["start": range.start, "duration": range.end - range.start]
74	            }
75	            // The sheet's Quality popup, in the core's own words: it resolves
76	            // a tier into these two keys and nothing else
77	            // (`ExportSheetController.overrides()`), so the agent spells them
78	            // the same way rather than re-deriving a rate from a tier name.
79	            // The core validates them — positive, u32 — and an unset key means
80	            // "the preset decides", which is what a nil bitrate already means
81	            // to the writer.
82	            if let video = try self.intArg(a, "video_bitrate") {
83	                overrides["video_bitrate"] = video
84	            }
85	            if let audio = try self.intArg(a, "audio_bitrate") {
86	                overrides["audio_bitrate"] = audio
87	            }
88	            // The sheet's Loudness popup, in the core's words again — and
89	            // through `doubleArg`, not `intArg`: −14.5 LUFS is a real request
90	            // and every one of these figures is a negative fraction. Neither
91	            // is validated here. `export_overrides.rs` owns the bounds
92	            // (−70…0 and −20…0) and names the offending value the way the
93	            // bitrate refusals do; either may come alone, the ceiling being
94	            // the master limiter's (spec §11 AU-27).
95	            // Restating a bound here would be a second spelling of it to
96	            // drift from the first.
97	            // The sheet sends both together and fixes the ceiling at
98	            // −1 dBTP; a caller that wants −0.3 or −2.0 says so here.
99	            if let target = try self.doubleArg(a, "loudness_lufs") {
100	                overrides["loudness_lufs"] = target
101	            }
102	            if let ceiling = try self.doubleArg(a, "peak_dbtp") {
103	                overrides["peak_dbtp"] = ceiling
104	            }
105	            // The sheet's Size popup: a row id, or "Custom…" as an explicit
106	            // [width, height]. Absent is no override at all, so the tool's
107	            // default and the sheet's are one code path in the core — the
108	            // document's size, or an image format's cap.
109	            if let size = try self.exportSizeArg(a, document.project, preset: presetID) {
110	                overrides["width"] = size.width
111	                overrides["height"] = size.height
112	            }
113	            // The sheet's Dynamic Range popup (spec §11 HD-14 (c)), forwarded
114	            // unread: the core's reader and resolver own its three words, its
115	            // per-row defaults and both refusals, each in its own sentence.
116	            if let range = a["dynamic_range"] {
117	                overrides["dynamic_range"] = range
118	            }
119	            // The sheet's Speed popup (spec §11 CX-12 (2)), forwarded unread on the
120	            // same terms: the core reads the three words and refuses a row without one.
121	            if let speed = a["encoder_speed"] {
122	                overrides["encoder_speed"] = speed
123	            }
124	            // The sheet's Bit depth popup (spec §11 AU-29), forwarded unread on the
125	            // same terms: the core reads 16 or 24 and refuses a row without a depth.
126	            if let bits = a["audio_bits"] {
127	                overrides["audio_bits"] = bits
128	            }
129	            // The sheet's Stems popup (spec §11 AU-108), forwarded unread on the same
130	            // terms: the core reads "tracks" or "names", refuses a movie row, and refuses
131	            // a project with no track heard.
132	            if let stems = a["stems"] {
133	                overrides["stems"] = stems
134	            }
135	            let settings: ExportSettings
136	            do {
137	                settings = try ReelExport.settings(
138	                    document.project, preset: presetID, overrides: overrides)
139	            } catch {
140	                throw Self.coreRefusal(error)
141	            }
142	            return (
143	                document, document.project, document.mediaURLs(), settings,
144	                GraphicRegistry.shared.snapshot(for: document.recipeKey)
145	            )
146	        }
147	        let (document, project, urls, settings, graphics) = prepared
148	        let url = try Self.requireFolder(
149	            of: Self.destinationURL(path, extension: Exporter.fileExtension(for: settings)))
150	
151	        // The graphics gate, here rather than only in the writer: a module
152	        // that does not compile refuses the CALL, so nothing is queued that
153	        // could only fail (`Exporter.graphicsRefusal`, the writer's own gate).
154	        if let refusal = Exporter.graphicsRefusal(
155	            project: project, settings: settings, graphics: graphics)
156	        {
157	            throw ToolError(message: refusal.localizedDescription)
158	        }
159	        let (id, status) = onMain { () -> (UInt64, String) in
160	            // The editor pauses before its own export so the player is not
161	            // decoding the same media; the agent's does the same.
162	            self.editor(document)?.playback.pause()
163	            let id = ExportQueueController.shared.enqueue(
164	                project: project, urls: urls, settings: settings, to: url, options: options,
165	                graphics: graphics)
166	            AgentExports.shared.track(
167	                id, settings: settings, burnInTimecode: options.burnInTimecode, started: started)
168	            let word = ExportQueueController.shared.job(id).map {
169	                Self.exportStatusWord($0.state)
170	            }
171	            return (id, word ?? "queued")
172	        }
173	        return try jsonResult(["export_id": id, "path": url.path, "status": status])
174	    }

176	    /// The `size` argument of `export`, in the Size popup's vocabulary: a row
177	    /// id resolved through the same `rc_export_sizes` the popup is built from
178	    /// (`document`, `preset`, `2160p`, `1440p`, `1080p`, `720p` — `ExportSize`
179	    /// in `ReelCore.swift` says what each means, and `core/src/export_size.rs`
180	    /// why every document lists every row), or the popup's "Custom…" as an
181	    /// explicit `[width, height]`. nil when absent, which is no override: the
182	    /// core's default for the preset.
183	    ///
184	    /// A value that is neither is refused by NAME, never read as absent — the
185	    /// rule every reader in `AgentServer+Arguments.swift` keeps, and the root
186	    /// `CLAUDE.md`'s: a value a handler cannot read is refused by name, never
187	    /// dropped. A `size` dropped in silence would export at the wrong size
188	    /// and report success. A custom
189	    /// size outside the sheet's own field range is refused the same way,
190	    /// where the sheet clamps: a tool has no field to clamp in view of the
191	    /// caller, and the sheet's reason — a mistyped digit must not reach the
192	    /// encoder as a 300 000-pixel frame — holds for a model's typo too.
193	    private func exportSizeArg(
194	        _ a: [String: Any], _ project: ReelProject, preset: String
195	    ) throws -> (width: Int, height: Int)? {
196	        guard let raw = a["size"], !(raw is NSNull) else { return nil }
197	        // The rows come first, whichever spelling follows: every refusal
198	        // below lists the ids from them rather than from a vocabulary
199	        // restated here, which could drift from the core's, and a preset the
200	        // core does not know is refused at this point in the same words
201	        // `exportProject` would use a call later.
202	        let rows: [ExportSize]
203	        do {
204	            rows = try ReelExport.sizes(project, preset: preset)
205	        } catch {
206	            throw Self.coreRefusal(error)
207	        }
208	        let ids = rows.map { $0.id }.joined(separator: ", ")
209	        if let id = raw as? String {
210	            guard let row = rows.first(where: { $0.id == id }) else {
211	                throw ToolError(
212	                    message: "No export size is called \"\(id)\" for \(preset). The sizes "
213	                        + "are: \(ids) — or pass [width, height].")
214	            }
215	            return (row.width, row.height)
216	        }
217	        if let array = raw as? [Any], array.count == 2 {
218	            let edges = array.compactMap(Self.wholeEdge)
219	            if edges.count == 2 {
220	                let range = ExportSheetController.sizeRange
221	                // Each refusal of a `size` offers the OTHER spelling: the
222	                // unknown-id one above names the custom form, and this one
223	                // names the rows, so a caller who meant a standard size and
224	                // reached for numbers has the ids in front of it.
225	                guard edges.allSatisfy(range.contains) else {
226	                    throw ToolError(
227	                        message: "A custom size must be \(range.lowerBound)…\(range.upperBound) "
228	                            + "px on each edge, not [\(edges[0]), \(edges[1])] — or pass a "
229	                            + "row: \(ids).")
230	                }
231	                return (edges[0], edges[1])
232	            }
233	        }
234	        throw ToolError(
235	            message: "size must be a row of the export sheet's Size popup — \(ids) — or "
236	                + "[width, height] in px, not \(Self.spelled(raw)).")
237	    }
238	
239	    /// One edge of a custom size as a whole number, or nil for a value that
240	    /// is not one — which sends the whole `size` to the refusal that names
241	    /// it. The coercion `intArg` applies holds: a string spelling of a whole
242	    /// number is a JSON-typing slip, not a different request. A fraction is
243	    /// refused rather than truncated, since 1920.5 is not a width the caller
244	    /// can have meant. So is a boolean: JSON's `true` arrives as an
245	    /// `NSNumber` like any other and would read as 1 through it, and the
246	    /// Core Foundation type is the one thing that still tells `true` from
247	    /// `1`.
248	    private static func wholeEdge(_ value: Any) -> Int? {
249	        if let number = value as? NSNumber {
250	            guard CFGetTypeID(number) != CFBooleanGetTypeID() else { return nil }
251	            let real = number.doubleValue
252	            return real.isFinite && real == real.rounded() ? number.intValue : nil
253	        }
254	        return (value as? String).flatMap(Int.init)
255	    }
256	
257	    /// A refusal from `rc_export_settings` or `rc_export_sizes` as the tool's
258	    /// error. The core's message passes through as it was, with one
259	    /// addition: an unknown preset id — the message that begins
260	    /// "unknown export preset", the same words from either call
261	    /// (`export.rs`) — gets the ids the table does take appended, because
262	    /// without them it is the one error a model cannot correct itself from,
263	    /// since nothing else lists the table. A refused bitrate or range keeps
264	    /// its own message alone: a list of presets under it would be a false
265	    /// lead.
266	    private static func coreRefusal(_ error: any Error) -> ToolError {
267	        let message = error.localizedDescription
268	        guard message.hasPrefix("unknown export preset") else {
269	            return ToolError(message: message)
270	        }
271	        let names = ReelExport.presets().map { $0.id }.joined(separator: ", ")
272	        return ToolError(message: "\(message). The presets are: \(names).")
273	    }
274	
275	    /// A caller's value as it was spelled, for a refusal that names it: its
276	    /// JSON where it is JSON, its Swift description otherwise.
277	    private static func spelled(_ raw: Any) -> String {
278	        guard JSONSerialization.isValidJSONObject([raw]),
279	            let data = try? JSONSerialization.data(
280	                withJSONObject: raw, options: [.fragmentsAllowed]),
281	            let text = String(data: data, encoding: .utf8)
282	        else { return String(describing: raw) }
283	        return text
284	    }
285	}

290	/// The agent's half of the Export Queue (spec §11 #326): `export` enqueues a
291	/// job in `ExportQueueController.shared` and answers its id at once, and the
292	/// two tools here follow it. `export_status` mirrors Window ▸ Export Queue's
293	/// row for that job (`ExportQueueWindowController`) — its state, its progress
294	/// bar, its phase and its closing sentence — and `cancel_export` mirrors the
295	/// row's Cancel button, which calls the same `ExportQueueController.cancel`.
296	///
297	/// **Only ids `export` returned are reachable.** A person's own queued job has
298	/// no record here and is answered as unknown: the mirror follows what the
299	/// agent started, not the queue as a whole.
300	///
301	/// **A record outlives its row.** The queue drops a finished job on Remove or
302	/// Clear Finished, and an agent that asks after that must still hear how it
303	/// ended, so `AgentExports` copies each tracked job's state on every queue
304	/// change — synchronously, on main, inside the queue's own post — and stamps
305	/// the finish (its time and the file's size) on its first terminal sight.
306	/// Records last for the launch and hold no project handle or graphic set.
307	extension AgentServer {
308	
309	    /// `export_status {export_id}` — the row of Window ▸ Export Queue for a job
310	    /// `export` started, read now; it never waits.
311	    func exportStatus(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
312	        let id = try exportIDArg(a)
313	        guard let status = AgentExports.shared.status(id) else {
314	            throw Self.unknownExport(id)
315	        }
316	        return try jsonResult(status)
317	    }
318	
319	    /// `cancel_export {export_id}` — the Export Queue row's Cancel. A queued
320	    /// or running job is cancelled through the queue (a running one answers
321	    /// through the writer, so it may still read `running` here); a finished
322	    /// one is left alone and answered as it is.
323	    func cancelExport(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
324	        let id = try exportIDArg(a)
325	        guard AgentExports.shared.status(id) != nil else {
326	            throw Self.unknownExport(id)
327	        }
328	        if let job = ExportQueueController.shared.job(id), !job.state.isFinished {
329	            ExportQueueController.shared.cancel(id)
330	        }
331	        guard let status = AgentExports.shared.status(id) else {
332	            throw Self.unknownExport(id)
333	        }
334	        return try jsonResult(status)
335	    }
336	
337	    /// The word a status answer spells a queue state with.
338	    static func exportStatusWord(_ state: ExportQueueController.State) -> String {
339	        switch state {
340	        case .waiting: return "queued"
341	        case .running: return "running"
342	        case .completed: return "done"
343	        case .failed: return "failed"
344	        case .cancelled: return "cancelled"
345	        }
346	    }

348	    /// `export_id`, required and whole. An id below 1 is no id `export`
349	    /// returned, so it is refused as an unknown one rather than converted.
350	    private func exportIDArg(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> UInt64 {
351	        guard let raw = try intArg(a, "export_id") else {
352	            throw ToolError(message: "Missing required argument: export_id")
353	        }
354	        guard raw >= 1 else {
355	            throw ToolError(
356	                message: "No export this launch has export_id \(raw) — ids come from export "
357	                    + "and last until Frame Job quits.")
358	        }
359	        return UInt64(raw)
360	    }
361	
362	    private static func unknownExport(_ id: UInt64) -> ToolError {
363	        ToolError(
364	            message: "No export this launch has export_id \(id) — ids come from export and "
365	                + "last until Frame Job quits.")
366	    }
367	}

369	/// What `AgentExports` keeps of one tracked job: the queue row's fields as
370	/// last seen, plus what the `done` answer needs that the job does not carry.
371	private struct AgentExportRecord {
372	    let settings: ExportSettings
373	    let burnInTimecode: Bool
374	    /// `systemUptime` at the `export` handler's first line.
375	    let started: TimeInterval
376	    var state: ExportQueueController.State
377	    var progress: Double
378	    var phase: String?
379	    var message: String?
380	    var destination: URL
381	    var loudness: ExportLoudness?
382	    var graphicWarnings: [ExportGraphicWarning]
383	    /// The media whose cursor file was not drawn (spec §11 CU-37 (c)).
384	    var cursorWarnings: [ExportCursorWarning]
385	    /// `systemUptime` at the first terminal sight, nil until then.
386	    var finished: TimeInterval?
387	    /// The file's size as read at that finish.
388	    var bytes: Int = 0
389	
390	    mutating func copy(_ job: ExportQueueController.Job) {
391	        state = job.state
392	        progress = job.progress
393	        phase = job.phase
394	        message = job.message
395	        destination = job.destination
396	        loudness = job.loudness
397	        graphicWarnings = job.graphicWarnings
398	        cursorWarnings = job.cursorWarnings
399	        guard job.state.isFinished, finished == nil else { return }
400	        finished = ProcessInfo.processInfo.systemUptime
401	        bytes =
402	            (try? FileManager.default.attributesOfItem(atPath: job.destination.path)[.size])
403	            .flatMap { ($0 as? NSNumber)?.intValue } ?? 0
404	    }

407	/// The records of every export the agent started this launch, by the queue's
408	/// job id. Main thread only, like the queue it reads.
409	final class AgentExports {
410	    static let shared = AgentExports()
411	
412	    private var records: [UInt64: AgentExportRecord] = [:]
413	    private var observer: NSObjectProtocol?
414	
415	    private init() {
416	        // `queue: nil` runs the block synchronously inside the queue's own
417	        // post, so a terminal state is copied before any Remove can drop it.
418	        observer = NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(
419	            forName: ExportQueueController.didChangeNotification,
420	            object: ExportQueueController.shared, queue: nil
421	        ) { [weak self] _ in self?.refresh() }
422	    }
423	
424	    /// Starts following a job `export` just enqueued. Reads it AT ONCE: an
425	    /// early refusal finishes inside `enqueue`, before this is called, so its
426	    /// terminal post has already gone by.
427	    func track(
428	        _ id: UInt64, settings: ExportSettings, burnInTimecode: Bool, started: TimeInterval
429	    ) {
430	        // Never nil: `enqueue` appends the job before it returns, an early
431	        // refusal only finishes it in place, and the only removals (`remove`,
432	        // `clearFinished`) are the queue window's button actions, which cannot
433	        // run inside the one main-thread block that enqueues and calls this.
434	        guard let job = ExportQueueController.shared.job(id) else { return }
435	        var record = AgentExportRecord(
436	            settings: settings, burnInTimecode: burnInTimecode, started: started,
437	            state: job.state, progress: job.progress, phase: job.phase, message: job.message,
438	            destination: job.destination, loudness: job.loudness,
439	            graphicWarnings: job.graphicWarnings, cursorWarnings: job.cursorWarnings)
440	        record.copy(job)
441	        records[id] = record
442	    }
443	
444	    /// The `export_status` answer for `id`, or nil for an id `export` never
445	    /// returned this launch.
446	    func status(_ id: UInt64) -> [String: Any]? {
447	        guard let record = records[id] else { return nil }
448	        let end = record.finished ?? ProcessInfo.processInfo.systemUptime
449	        var answer: [String: Any] = [:]
450	        switch record.state {
451	        case .running:
452	            answer["progress"] = record.progress
453	            if let phase = record.phase { answer["phase"] = phase }
454	        case .completed:
455	            answer = AgentServer.exportResult(
456	                settings: record.settings, burnInTimecode: record.burnInTimecode,
457	                path: record.destination.path, bytes: record.bytes, loudness: record.loudness,
458	                graphicWarnings: record.graphicWarnings, cursorWarnings: record.cursorWarnings)
459	        case .failed, .cancelled:
460	            answer["reason"] = record.message ?? ""
461	        case .waiting:
462	            // The memory hold's sentence, present only while held (spec §11 CX-18).
463	            if let held = record.message { answer["waiting"] = held }
464	        }
465	        if record.state == .waiting || record.state == .running,
466	            let seconds = ExportEncoderCosts.estimatedSeconds(for: record.settings)
467	        {
468	            answer["estimated_seconds"] = Int(seconds.rounded())
469	        }
470	        answer["export_id"] = id
471	        answer["status"] = AgentServer.exportStatusWord(record.state)
472	        answer["path"] = record.destination.path
473	        answer["elapsed"] = ((end - record.started) * 1000).rounded() / 1000
474	        return answer
475	    }
476	
477	    /// Copies every unfinished tracked job from the queue.
478	    private func refresh() {
479	        let queue = ExportQueueController.shared
480	        for (id, record) in records where record.finished == nil {
481	            guard let job = queue.job(id) else { continue }
482	            var updated = record
483	            updated.copy(job)
484	            records[id] = updated
485	        }
486	    }
487	}

490	/// What a finished export's answer carries: the resolved settings and the
491	/// facts about the file that was written, read off the queue's job once it
492	/// has finished — `export_status`'s `done` answer
493	/// (`AgentServer+ExportStatus.swift`), which since spec §11 #326 is what
494	/// `export` itself answered before it returned at once.
495	extension AgentServer {
496	
497	    /// The `done` answer's keys, exactly the ones `export` answered when it
498	    /// blocked to the file. `bytes` is the file's size as read at the finish.
499	    static func exportResult(
500	        settings: ExportSettings, burnInTimecode: Bool, path: String, bytes: Int,
501	        loudness: ExportLoudness?, graphicWarnings: [ExportGraphicWarning],
502	        cursorWarnings: [ExportCursorWarning]
503	    ) -> [String: Any] {
504	        var result: [String: Any] = [
505	            "ok": true,
506	            "path": path,
507	            "bytes": bytes,
508	            "preset": settings.preset,
509	            "container": settings.container,
510	            "codec": settings.codec,
511	            "width": settings.width,
512	            "height": settings.height,
513	            "fps": [settings.fps.num, settings.fps.den],
514	            "start": settings.start,
515	            "duration": settings.duration,
516	            // Not one of the resolved settings — the core never saw it — but
517	            // it is a fact about the file that was written, and every other
518	            // key here is one too.
519	            //
520	            // What it establishes is exactly one link and not the chain: this
521	            // is `options.burnInTimecode`, the local decoded a few lines up,
522	            // so a caller reading it back knows the argument was READ rather
523	            // than dropped in argument reading — the failure `boolArg`'s
524	            // refusal covers from the other side. It does NOT say the writer
525	            // used it; only a pixel can say that, and
526	            // `tools/proof/phase7_proof.py` is where one does.
527	            "burn_in_timecode": burnInTimecode,
528	        ]
529	        // The picture an HLG project's file was written as (`hlg`, `pq` or
530	        // `sdr`); absent for every SDR project and audio row.
531	        if let color = settings.color {
532	            result["dynamic_range"] = color
533	        }
534	        // The speed the `av1` row was encoded at (spec §11 CX-12 (2)); absent elsewhere.
535	        if let speed = settings.encoderSpeed {
536	            result["encoder_speed"] = speed.rawValue
537	        }
538	        // The depth a WAV or AIFF was written at (spec §11 AU-29); absent elsewhere.
539	        if let bits = settings.audioBits {
540	            result["audio_bits"] = bits
541	        }
542	        // Each stem written beside the mix, in order (spec §11 AU-108); absent without.
543	        if !settings.stems.isEmpty {
544	            let mix = URL(fileURLWithPath: path)
545	            result["stems"] = settings.stems.map {
546	                [
547	                    "name": $0.name, "tracks": $0.tracks,
548	                    "path": ExportStemsPipeline.url(for: $0, mix: mix).path,
549	                ] as [String: Any]
550	            }
551	        }
552	        if let measured = loudnessResult(loudness) {
553	            result["loudness"] = measured
554	        }
555	        if let warned = graphicWarningsResult(graphicWarnings) {
556	            result["graphic_warnings"] = warned
557	        }
558	        if let warned = cursorWarningsResult(cursorWarnings) {
559	            result["cursor_warnings"] = warned
560	        }
561	        return result
562	    }
563	
564	    /// What the export's sound MEASURED, for the result — nil, and then the
565	    /// key is simply absent, wherever `Exporter` published no report: a
566	    /// format that holds no audio track at all (GIF and APNG), and a
567	    /// timeline with no sound in it, which is the case a caller actually
568	    /// meets. A missing `loudness` is therefore "there was nothing to
569	    /// measure", never "the measurement was skipped".
570	    ///
571	    /// This is `detect_silence`'s posture applied to the writer: the numbers
572	    /// are read back off the file's own mix rather than repeated from the
573	    /// request, so a caller can check that a −14 LUFS export actually landed
574	    /// at −14, which is what makes phase 5's ±0.5 LU claim a claim anyone can
575	    /// test over MCP. `target` is what was ASKED for and is absent when
576	    /// nothing was — every export measures itself and reports, normalised or
577	    /// not.
578	    ///
579	    /// It is read off the queue's job (`ExportQueueController.Job.loudness`),
580	    /// which `finished` copies from the `Exporter` before dropping it:
581	    /// `Exporter.finish` publishes the report before it calls back, so every
582	    /// consumer (this, the queue's row and the progress sheet) reads it after
583	    /// the completion has fired.
584	    ///
585	    /// Every level goes through `jsonLevel`: a silent programme measures
586	    /// −∞ dBTP, and `JSONSerialization` throws on an infinity — which would
587	    /// report a successful export as a failed tool call.
588	    static func loudnessResult(_ report: ExportLoudness?) -> [String: Any]? {
589	        guard let report = report else { return nil }
590	        var measured: [String: Any] = [
591	            // The same sentence the progress sheet's last line shows, so the
592	            // two consumers of one measurement cannot describe it differently.
593	            "summary": report.summary,
594	            "true_peak_dbtp": jsonLevel(report.truePeakDBTP),
595	            // The shifted sample peak, never above the true peak the master
596	            // held (spec §11 AU-28).
597	            "sample_peak_dbfs": jsonLevel(
598	                min(report.measured.samplePeakDBFS + report.gainDB, report.truePeakDBTP)),
599	            "gain_db": report.gainDB,
600	            "ceiling_dbtp": jsonLevel(report.ceiling),
601	            "limited_db": report.limitedDB,
602	            "capped_by_gain": report.cappedByGain,
603	        ]
604	        // Absent rather than null, and for a reason worth the line: a
605	        // programme shorter than one 400 ms gating block, or one whose every
606	        // block fell under the standard's absolute gate, HAS no integrated
607	        // loudness. `summary` says so in words.
608	        if let integrated = report.integratedLUFS, integrated.isFinite {
609	            measured["integrated_lufs"] = integrated
610	        }
611	        if let target = report.target {
612	            measured["target_lufs"] = target
613	        }
614	        return measured
615	    }

413	    /// names, so a test can diff it or a human can open it.
414	    ///
415	    /// **The write is `FrameWriter`'s, and that is the point of it** (road map
416	    /// 2's phase 7a). This handler used to hold its own
417	    /// `CGImageDestination` — which made File ▸ Save Frame… and this tool two
418	    /// encoders that happened to agree — and now both call one `writeFrame`
419	    /// (it labels the frame BT.709, spec §11 PR-11). That
420	    /// is what makes "Save Frame's PNG is byte-identical to `render_frame`'s"
421	    /// a fact about the code rather than a claim, and it is the only way the
422	    /// line can ever be checked: a save panel cannot be driven over MCP or
423	    /// offscreen, so no proof script can press the menu item.
424	    ///
425	    /// **The last sentence of the text block is load-bearing.** A call that
426	    /// names neither `path` nor `format` still writes a PNG into the
427	    /// temporary directory and still ends "Written to <path>." byte for byte
428	    /// as it did before this phase: five proof scripts (phases 1, 2, 3, 4 and
429	    /// 6) read the path back out of it with `Written to (\S+\.png)\.` and
430	    /// every PNG comparison this project makes hangs off that one regular
431	    /// expression. Anything new to say goes BEFORE it.
432	    ///
433	    /// **`burn_in_timecode` is a recipe option and never an export override**
434	    /// (`RecipeOptions`): it changes the picture, so it travels with the
435	    /// description of the picture. It is here for parity with `export`, and
436	    /// because a burn-in lives only in rendered pixels — this is the one tool
437	    /// that can photograph one, so it is the instrument every claim about
438	    /// phase 7c's layer is made through.
439	    ///
440	    /// **`ungraded` and the four scope booleans are View ▸ Show Ungraded's
441	    /// and View ▸ Scopes' mirror** (spec §11 GR-4, GR-5, GR-10): the switch,
442	    /// the panel and its slot picks are view state and never reach this tool,
443	    /// so it is asked here. `ungraded` is a recipe option like
444	    /// `burn_in_timecode`; `waveform`, `parade`, `vectorscope` and `histogram`
445	    /// measure the frame just written through the panel's own analyser, once
446	    /// for all of them, and write each beside the image as
447	    /// `<path>.<scope>.json` with a sentence each, in that order
448	    /// (`writeScopes`, in `AgentServer+Scopes.swift`). `vectorscope_zoom`
449	    /// (1, 2 or 4, spec §11 GR-31) is a slot's zoom cells' mirror: the
450	    /// vectorscope counted at that zoom. Anything else is refused by name,
451	    /// and so is the zoom without `vectorscope: true`, both before the render.
452	    ///
453	    /// **`sdr_version` is View ▸ Show SDR Version's mirror** (spec §11 HD-7,
454	    /// HD-14): an HLG project's SDR version, a recipe option like `ungraded`;
455	    /// a JPEG of an HLG project is drawn so too, and an SDR project's frame is
456	    /// unchanged by it.
457	    ///
458	    /// **`selection` is View ▸ Show Selection's mirror** (spec §11 GR-13): an
459	    /// adjustment clip's id, a recipe option like `ungraded` — the clip's
460	    /// qualifier drawn as grey, every layer in front of it left out, black
461	    /// where the clip is not on the frame. An id naming no adjustment clip of
462	    /// the edited project is refused, naming `selection`.
463	    ///
464	    /// **A cut-out clip waits for its masks** (spec §11 CO-22 (f)): up to
465	    /// `Exporter.frameCutoutWait` (30 s), then drawn uncut and named, one
466	    /// sentence per clip just before the last.
467	    ///
468	    /// **A graphic that warned or failed is named** (G-8, G3c): one sentence
469	    /// per report the frame's pin held, before the last. The set is the
470	    /// DOCUMENT's (`recipeKey`), not the scoped handle's: a nest draws the
471	    /// package's modules too.
472	    func renderFrame(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
473	        let selection = try selectionArg(a)
474	        let context = try onMain {
475	            () throws -> (ReelProject, [UInt32: URL], Ticks, CGSize, GraphicSet?) in
476	            let document = try self.target(a)
477	            let t = try self.optionalTimeArg(a, "t", document) ?? document.playhead
478	            if let selection, !(document.editedProject.snapshot.clip(selection)
479	                .map(InspectorTab.isAdjustment) ?? false)
480	            {
481	                throw ToolError(
482	                    message: "selection must name an adjustment clip of this project; clip "
483	                        + "\(selection) is not one.")
484	            }
485	            // `editedProject`, not `project` — road map 2's phase 9. With a
486	            // nest open (`set_scope`) this renders THAT nest at its own
487	            // frozen canvas, from its own zero, with the outer transform not
488	            // applied: the same picture the preview panel is showing, which
489	            // is what makes a scoped edit checkable at all. It is the one
490	            // place in this file that side of the split is taken; `export`
491	            // below stays the DOCUMENT's, because an export writes the whole
492	            // timeline whatever the timeline happens to be showing. With no
493	            // nest open the two are the same handle and every earlier
494	            // phase's frame comparison is unaffected.
495	            return (
496	                document.editedProject, document.mediaURLs(), max(0, t),
497	                document.editedProject.snapshot.canvas.size,
498	                GraphicRegistry.shared.snapshot(for: document.recipeKey)
499	            )
500	        }
501	        let (project, urls, time, canvasSize, graphics) = context
502	        var maxWidth: Int?
503	        if let requested = try intArg(a, "max_width") {
504	            guard requested >= 16, requested <= 8192 else {
505	                throw ToolError(message: "max_width must be 16…8192 px (got \(requested)).")
506	            }
507	            maxWidth = requested
508	        }
509	        let burnIn = try boolArg(a, "burn_in_timecode") ?? false
510	        let ungraded = try boolArg(a, "ungraded") ?? false
511	        let sdrVersion = try boolArg(a, "sdr_version") ?? false
512	        var scopes: [ScopeKind] = []
513	        for kind in ScopeKind.allCases where try boolArg(a, kind.rawValue) ?? false {
514	            scopes.append(kind)
515	        }
516	        let vectorscopeZoom = try vectorscopeZoomArg(a, measured: scopes.contains(.vectorscope))
517	        // Resolved BEFORE the render, so a mistyped folder is answered in a
518	        // millisecond rather than after a decode: `exportProject` orders its
519	        // own two the same way.
520	        let (url, format) = try frameDestination(a, at: time)
521	        // View ▸ Show SDR Version's mirror, and a JPEG of an HLG project, draw
522	        // its SDR version (spec §11 HD-14 (e), (g)); an SDR project's frame is
523	        // its own SDR version, the recipe unchanged.
524	        let output = project.snapshot.canvas.output
525	        let options = RecipeOptions(
526	            burnInTimecode: burnIn, ungraded: ungraded, selection: selection,
527	            dynamicRange: sdrVersion ? .sdr : nil
528	        ).forFrame(format, output: output)
529	        // Off the main thread by construction — `Exporter.renderFrame` opens
530	        // asset tracks and decodes, and says so. A PNG or HEIC keeps depth, so
531	        // `Exporter` reads a frame showing a deep still or a deep VP9 track
532	        // through the reader (spec §11 PR-9, PR-12); Save Frame passes the same.
533	        let rendered = Exporter.renderFrameReported(
534	            project: project, urls: urls, at: time, maxWidth: maxWidth, options: options,
535	            graphics: graphics, keepsDepth: format.carriesDepth,
536	            cutoutWait: Exporter.frameCutoutWait)
537	        guard let image = rendered.image else {
538	            throw ToolError(
539	                message: "No frame at \(time). Either the time is past the end of the timeline, "
540	                    + "the media is missing, or the timeline is empty.")
541	        }
542	        do {
543	            try FrameWriter.writeFrame(image, as: format, to: url)
544	        } catch {
545	            // `FrameWriter.WriteError` names the path and the format in every
546	            // case it has, so the message passes through as it was written.
547	            throw ToolError(message: error.localizedDescription)
548	        }
549	        guard let data = try? Data(contentsOf: url) else {
550	            throw ToolError(message: "Wrote \(url.path) but could not read it back.")
551	        }
552	        var text =
553	            "Frame at \(time) ticks of a \(Int(canvasSize.width))×\(Int(canvasSize.height)) px "
554	            + "canvas, rendered at \(image.width)×\(image.height) px"
555	        if options.burnInTimecode {
556	            text += ", with the project timecode burnt in"
557	        }
558	        if options.ungraded {
559	            text += ", with every grade removed"
560	        }
561	        if let selection {
562	            text += ", drawn as clip \(selection)'s qualifier selection (white fully graded, "
563	                + "black untouched)"
564	        }
565	        if output == .hlg, options.dynamicRange == .sdr {
566	            text += ", as the project's SDR version"
567	        }
568	        text += "."
569	        // Said where the caller can see it rather than only in the schema: a
570	        // frame off a transparent canvas (phase 7b) has just lost its alpha,
571	        // and a note that arrives with the file is the one that is read.
572	        if !format.carriesAlpha {
573	            text += " " + FrameWriter.flattenNote
574	        }
575	        for report in rendered.graphics {
576	            text += " " + Self.graphicSentence(report)
577	        }
578	        // A cursor file the frame could not draw (spec §11 CU-37 (c)).
579	        for sentence in Exporter.cursorSentences(rendered.cursorWarnings) {
580	            text += " " + sentence
581	        }
582	        if !scopes.isEmpty {
583	            // The scopes read the frame drawn (spec §11 HD-15 (a), (b)): an HLG
584	            // project's own picture as HLG, its SDR version (and a JPEG) as SDR.
585	            let signal = ScopeSignal(output: output, dynamicRange: options.dynamicRange)
586	            text += " " + (try Self.writeScopes(
587	                scopes, vectorscopeZoom: vectorscopeZoom, signal: signal, of: image, beside: url))
588	        }
589	        // A cut-out clip whose masks were not ready within the wait (spec §11 CO-22 (f)); a
590	        // picture cut by its foreground names its foreground masks (CO-106).
591	        let foreground = Set(
592	            (project.snapshot.clips + project.snapshot.nests.flatMap(\.clips))
593	                .filter { CutoutWants.kind(of: $0) == .foreground }.map(\.id))
594	        for sentence in Exporter.cutoutSentences(rendered.uncut, foreground: foreground) {
595	            text += " " + sentence
596	        }
597	        text += " Written to \(url.path)."
598	        return try callResult(
599	            content: [
600	                [
601	                    "type": "image", "data": data.base64EncodedString(),
602	                    "mimeType": Self.mimeType(format),
603	                ],
604	                ["type": "text", "text": text],
605	            ], isError: false)
606	    }

608	    /// One graphic's report as `render_frame` says it: failed at a frame,
609	    /// did not compile, or warned — each diagnostic with its location.
610	    static func graphicSentence(_ report: GraphicReport) -> String {
611	        let said = report.diagnostics.map { $0.located }.joined(separator: "; ")
612	        guard let frame = report.frame else {
613	            return "Graphic \"\(report.name)\" does not compile: \(said)."
614	        }
615	        let verb = report.failed ? "failed" : "warned"
616	        return "Graphic \"\(report.name)\" \(verb) at frame \(frame): \(said)."
617	    }
618	
619	    /// Where `render_frame` writes and in what container — its `path` and
620	    /// `format` arguments resolved together, because neither can be read
621	    /// without the other.
622	    ///
623	    /// **No `path` is the case every proof script takes**, and it is exactly
624	    /// what it was: a file in the temporary directory named for the tick it
625	    /// holds, ending in the format's own extension — `.png` unless a caller
626	    /// asked for something else.
627	    ///
628	    /// With a `path`, the format is `FrameWriter`'s answer and not a second
629	    /// opinion: an explicit `format` wins, else the path's own extension, else
630	    /// PNG — `export_captions`' rule, one file over. The path then goes
631	    /// through `destinationURL`, so a wrong extension is REPLACED rather than
632	    /// appended to: `{path: "shot.jpg", format: "png"}` writes `shot.png`, not
633	    /// the doubled `shot.jpg.png`, which is why the five image containers
634	    /// joined `replaceableExtensions` in this phase.
635	    ///
636	    /// The folder must already exist and is refused BY NAME when it does not,
637	    /// which is `export`'s posture at the same point: a tool that created
638	    /// directories would answer a mistyped path by scattering empty ones.
639	    private func frameDestination(
640	        _ a: [String: Any], at time: Ticks
641	    ) throws -> (url: URL, format: FrameWriter.Format) {
642	        let requested = try requestedFrameFormat(a)
643	        guard let given = try stringArg(a, "path") else {
644	            let format = requested ?? .png
645	            return (
646	                Self.temporaryOutput("framejob-frame-\(time)", extension: format.fileExtension),
647	                format
648	            )
649	        }
650	        let path = try Self.nonEmptyOutputPath(given)
651	        let format = FrameWriter.format(
652	            for: URL(fileURLWithPath: (path as NSString).expandingTildeInPath),
653	            requested: requested)
654	        let url = try Self.requireFolder(
655	            of: Self.destinationURL(path, extension: format.fileExtension))
656	        return (url, format)
657	    }
658	
659	    /// The `format` argument, refused BY NAME when it names no container —
660	    /// nil when it is absent, which is what lets `FrameWriter.format(for:)`
661	    /// fall back to the path. It is `export_captions`' `requestedFormat` with
662	    /// three rows instead of two.
663	    ///
664	    /// `jpg` is read as `jpeg` on purpose. `FrameWriter.Format`'s raw value is
665	    /// deliberately NOT its file extension — JPEG has two spellings and
666	    /// collapsing them would make one of them wrong — and `format(for:)`
667	    /// already reads both off a path, so refusing four letters here that are
668	    /// accepted in the argument beside it is an inconsistency a caller meets
669	    /// on its first try. The schema still advertises the three canonical
670	    /// names, which is what a caller reading the catalog will send.
671	    private func requestedFrameFormat(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> FrameWriter.Format? {
672	        guard let name = try stringArg(a, "format") else { return nil }
673	        let lowered = name.lowercased()
674	        guard let format = FrameWriter.Format(rawValue: lowered == "jpg" ? "jpeg" : lowered)
675	        else {
676	            let known = FrameWriter.Format.allCases.map { $0.rawValue }
677	            throw ToolError(
678	                message: "format must be one of " + known.joined(separator: ", ")
679	                    + " (got \"\(name)\").")
680	        }
681	        return format
682	    }
683	
684	    /// The image block's `mimeType`, read off the format's own `UTType`
685	    /// rather than switched over a second time here: the block and the file
686	    /// are then one decision, and a fourth container would arrive described
687	    /// correctly without anybody remembering this line.
688	    ///
689	    /// All three carry one (measured: `image/png`, `image/jpeg`,
690	    /// `image/heic`). The fallback exists only because the API is optional,
691	    /// and it is deliberately generic rather than a guess: telling a client
692	    /// that a HEIC is a PNG is worse than telling it nothing.
693	    private static func mimeType(_ format: FrameWriter.Format) -> String {
694	        format.contentType.preferredMIMEType ?? "application/octet-stream"
695	    }
696	}

13	    /// that go to the same `Exporter.export` the sheet uses: there is exactly
14	    /// one writer, so an agent export and a menu export cannot disagree.
15	    ///
16	    /// Answers AT ONCE (spec §11 #326): every refusal is made here, before
17	    /// anything is queued — the arguments, the core's settings, the folder
18	    /// and the graphics gate — and the export is then a job in the Export
19	    /// Queue, exactly as the sheet's Add to Queue makes one, answered as
20	    /// `{export_id, path, status}`. `export_status` follows the job and
21	    /// `cancel_export` stops it (`AgentServer+ExportStatus.swift`); a failure
22	    /// while writing comes back from there. The queue window is not shown.

25	    /// `burn_in_timecode` is a recipe option (`RecipeOptions`), read below

179	    /// in `ReelCore.swift` says what each means, and `core/src/export_size.rs`

181	    /// explicit `[width, height]`. nil when absent, which is no override: the
182	    /// core's default for the preset.
183	    ///
184	    /// A value that is neither is refused by NAME, never read as absent — the
185	    /// rule every reader in `AgentServer+Arguments.swift` keeps, and the root
186	    /// `CLAUDE.md`'s: a value a handler cannot read is refused by name, never
187	    /// dropped. A `size` dropped in silence would export at the wrong size
188	    /// and report success. A custom
189	    /// size outside the sheet's own field range is refused the same way,
190	    /// where the sheet clamps: a tool has no field to clamp in view of the
191	    /// caller, and the sheet's reason — a mistyped digit must not reach the
192	    /// encoder as a 300 000-pixel frame — holds for a model's typo too.
193	    private func exportSizeArg(
194	        _ a: [String: Any], _ project: ReelProject, preset: String
195	    ) throws -> (width: Int, height: Int)? {
196	        guard let raw = a["size"], !(raw is NSNull) else { return nil }
197	        // The rows come first, whichever spelling follows: every refusal
198	        // below lists the ids from them rather than from a vocabulary
199	        // restated here, which could drift from the core's, and a preset the
200	        // core does not know is refused at this point in the same words
201	        // `exportProject` would use a call later.
202	        let rows: [ExportSize]
203	        do {
204	            rows = try ReelExport.sizes(project, preset: preset)
205	        } catch {
206	            throw Self.coreRefusal(error)
207	        }
208	        let ids = rows.map { $0.id }.joined(separator: ", ")
209	        if let id = raw as? String {
210	            guard let row = rows.first(where: { $0.id == id }) else {
211	                throw ToolError(
212	                    message: "No export size is called \"\(id)\" for \(preset). The sizes "
213	                        + "are: \(ids) — or pass [width, height].")
214	            }
215	            return (row.width, row.height)
216	        }
217	        if let array = raw as? [Any], array.count == 2 {
218	            let edges = array.compactMap(Self.wholeEdge)
219	            if edges.count == 2 {
220	                let range = ExportSheetController.sizeRange
221	                // Each refusal of a `size` offers the OTHER spelling: the
222	                // unknown-id one above names the custom form, and this one
223	                // names the rows, so a caller who meant a standard size and
224	                // reached for numbers has the ids in front of it.
225	                guard edges.allSatisfy(range.contains) else {
226	                    throw ToolError(
227	                        message: "A custom size must be \(range.lowerBound)…\(range.upperBound) "
228	                            + "px on each edge, not [\(edges[0]), \(edges[1])] — or pass a "
229	                            + "row: \(ids).")
230	                }
231	                return (edges[0], edges[1])
232	            }
233	        }
234	        throw ToolError(
235	            message: "size must be a row of the export sheet's Size popup — \(ids) — or "
236	                + "[width, height] in px, not \(Self.spelled(raw)).")
237	    }
238	
239	    /// One edge of a custom size as a whole number, or nil for a value that
240	    /// is not one — which sends the whole `size` to the refusal that names
241	    /// it. The coercion `intArg` applies holds: a string spelling of a whole
242	    /// number is a JSON-typing slip, not a different request. A fraction is
243	    /// refused rather than truncated, since 1920.5 is not a width the caller
244	    /// can have meant. So is a boolean: JSON's `true` arrives as an
245	    /// `NSNumber` like any other and would read as 1 through it, and the
246	    /// Core Foundation type is the one thing that still tells `true` from
247	    /// `1`.
248	    private static func wholeEdge(_ value: Any) -> Int? {
249	        if let number = value as? NSNumber {
250	            guard CFGetTypeID(number) != CFBooleanGetTypeID() else { return nil }
251	            let real = number.doubleValue
252	            return real.isFinite && real == real.rounded() ? number.intValue : nil
253	        }
254	        return (value as? String).flatMap(Int.init)
255	    }
256	
257	    /// A refusal from `rc_export_settings` or `rc_export_sizes` as the tool's
258	    /// error. The core's message passes through as it was, with one
259	    /// addition: an unknown preset id — the message that begins
260	    /// "unknown export preset", the same words from either call
261	    /// (`export.rs`) — gets the ids the table does take appended, because
262	    /// without them it is the one error a model cannot correct itself from,
263	    /// since nothing else lists the table. A refused bitrate or range keeps
264	    /// its own message alone: a list of presets under it would be a false
265	    /// lead.
266	    private static func coreRefusal(_ error: any Error) -> ToolError {
267	        let message = error.localizedDescription
268	        guard message.hasPrefix("unknown export preset") else {
269	            return ToolError(message: message)
270	        }
271	        let names = ReelExport.presets().map { $0.id }.joined(separator: ", ")
272	        return ToolError(message: "\(message). The presets are: \(names).")
273	    }
274	
275	    /// A caller's value as it was spelled, for a refusal that names it: its
276	    /// JSON where it is JSON, its Swift description otherwise.
277	    private static func spelled(_ raw: Any) -> String {
278	        guard JSONSerialization.isValidJSONObject([raw]),
279	            let data = try? JSONSerialization.data(
280	                withJSONObject: raw, options: [.fragmentsAllowed]),
281	            let text = String(data: data, encoding: .utf8)
282	        else { return String(describing: raw) }
283	        return text
284	    }
285	}

290	/// The agent's half of the Export Queue (spec §11 #326): `export` enqueues a
291	/// job in `ExportQueueController.shared` and answers its id at once, and the
292	/// two tools here follow it. `export_status` mirrors Window ▸ Export Queue's
293	/// row for that job (`ExportQueueWindowController`) — its state, its progress
294	/// bar, its phase and its closing sentence — and `cancel_export` mirrors the
295	/// row's Cancel button, which calls the same `ExportQueueController.cancel`.
296	///
297	/// **Only ids `export` returned are reachable.** A person's own queued job has
298	/// no record here and is answered as unknown: the mirror follows what the
299	/// agent started, not the queue as a whole.
300	///
301	/// **A record outlives its row.** The queue drops a finished job on Remove or
302	/// Clear Finished, and an agent that asks after that must still hear how it
303	/// ended, so `AgentExports` copies each tracked job's state on every queue
304	/// change — synchronously, on main, inside the queue's own post — and stamps
305	/// the finish (its time and the file's size) on its first terminal sight.
306	/// Records last for the launch and hold no project handle or graphic set.
307	extension AgentServer {
308	
309	    /// `export_status {export_id}` — the row of Window ▸ Export Queue for a job
310	    /// `export` started, read now; it never waits.
311	    func exportStatus(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
312	        let id = try exportIDArg(a)
313	        guard let status = AgentExports.shared.status(id) else {
314	            throw Self.unknownExport(id)
315	        }
316	        return try jsonResult(status)
317	    }
318	
319	    /// `cancel_export {export_id}` — the Export Queue row's Cancel. A queued
320	    /// or running job is cancelled through the queue (a running one answers
321	    /// through the writer, so it may still read `running` here); a finished
322	    /// one is left alone and answered as it is.
323	    func cancelExport(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
324	        let id = try exportIDArg(a)
325	        guard AgentExports.shared.status(id) != nil else {
326	            throw Self.unknownExport(id)
327	        }
328	        if let job = ExportQueueController.shared.job(id), !job.state.isFinished {
329	            ExportQueueController.shared.cancel(id)
330	        }
331	        guard let status = AgentExports.shared.status(id) else {
332	            throw Self.unknownExport(id)
333	        }
334	        return try jsonResult(status)
335	    }
336	
337	    /// The word a status answer spells a queue state with.
338	    static func exportStatusWord(_ state: ExportQueueController.State) -> String {
339	        switch state {
340	        case .waiting: return "queued"
341	        case .running: return "running"
342	        case .completed: return "done"
343	        case .failed: return "failed"
344	        case .cancelled: return "cancelled"
345	        }
346	    }
347	
348	    /// `export_id`, required and whole. An id below 1 is no id `export`
349	    /// returned, so it is refused as an unknown one rather than converted.
350	    private func exportIDArg(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> UInt64 {
351	        guard let raw = try intArg(a, "export_id") else {
352	            throw ToolError(message: "Missing required argument: export_id")
353	        }
354	        guard raw >= 1 else {
355	            throw ToolError(
356	                message: "No export this launch has export_id \(raw) — ids come from export "
357	                    + "and last until Frame Job quits.")
358	        }
359	        return UInt64(raw)
360	    }
361	
362	    private static func unknownExport(_ id: UInt64) -> ToolError {
363	        ToolError(
364	            message: "No export this launch has export_id \(id) — ids come from export and "
365	                + "last until Frame Job quits.")
366	    }
367	}

369	/// What `AgentExports` keeps of one tracked job: the queue row's fields as
370	/// last seen, plus what the `done` answer needs that the job does not carry.
371	private struct AgentExportRecord {
372	    let settings: ExportSettings
373	    let burnInTimecode: Bool
374	    /// `systemUptime` at the `export` handler's first line.
375	    let started: TimeInterval
376	    var state: ExportQueueController.State
377	    var progress: Double
378	    var phase: String?
379	    var message: String?
380	    var destination: URL
381	    var loudness: ExportLoudness?
382	    var graphicWarnings: [ExportGraphicWarning]
383	    /// The media whose cursor file was not drawn (spec §11 CU-37 (c)).
384	    var cursorWarnings: [ExportCursorWarning]
385	    /// `systemUptime` at the first terminal sight, nil until then.
386	    var finished: TimeInterval?
387	    /// The file's size as read at that finish.
388	    var bytes: Int = 0
389	
390	    mutating func copy(_ job: ExportQueueController.Job) {
391	        state = job.state
392	        progress = job.progress
393	        phase = job.phase
394	        message = job.message
395	        destination = job.destination
396	        loudness = job.loudness
397	        graphicWarnings = job.graphicWarnings
398	        cursorWarnings = job.cursorWarnings
399	        guard job.state.isFinished, finished == nil else { return }
400	        finished = ProcessInfo.processInfo.systemUptime
401	        bytes =
402	            (try? FileManager.default.attributesOfItem(atPath: job.destination.path)[.size])
403	            .flatMap { ($0 as? NSNumber)?.intValue } ?? 0
404	    }
405	}

407	/// The records of every export the agent started this launch, by the queue's
408	/// job id. Main thread only, like the queue it reads.
409	final class AgentExports {
410	    static let shared = AgentExports()
411	
412	    private var records: [UInt64: AgentExportRecord] = [:]
413	    private var observer: NSObjectProtocol?
414	
415	    private init() {
416	        // `queue: nil` runs the block synchronously inside the queue's own
417	        // post, so a terminal state is copied before any Remove can drop it.
418	        observer = NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(
419	            forName: ExportQueueController.didChangeNotification,
420	            object: ExportQueueController.shared, queue: nil
421	        ) { [weak self] _ in self?.refresh() }
422	    }
423	
424	    /// Starts following a job `export` just enqueued. Reads it AT ONCE: an
425	    /// early refusal finishes inside `enqueue`, before this is called, so its
426	    /// terminal post has already gone by.
427	    func track(
428	        _ id: UInt64, settings: ExportSettings, burnInTimecode: Bool, started: TimeInterval
429	    ) {
430	        // Never nil: `enqueue` appends the job before it returns, an early
431	        // refusal only finishes it in place, and the only removals (`remove`,
432	        // `clearFinished`) are the queue window's button actions, which cannot
433	        // run inside the one main-thread block that enqueues and calls this.
434	        guard let job = ExportQueueController.shared.job(id) else { return }
435	        var record = AgentExportRecord(
436	            settings: settings, burnInTimecode: burnInTimecode, started: started,
437	            state: job.state, progress: job.progress, phase: job.phase, message: job.message,
438	            destination: job.destination, loudness: job.loudness,
439	            graphicWarnings: job.graphicWarnings, cursorWarnings: job.cursorWarnings)
440	        record.copy(job)
441	        records[id] = record
442	    }
443	
444	    /// The `export_status` answer for `id`, or nil for an id `export` never
445	    /// returned this launch.
446	    func status(_ id: UInt64) -> [String: Any]? {
447	        guard let record = records[id] else { return nil }
448	        let end = record.finished ?? ProcessInfo.processInfo.systemUptime
449	        var answer: [String: Any] = [:]
450	        switch record.state {
451	        case .running:
452	            answer["progress"] = record.progress
453	            if let phase = record.phase { answer["phase"] = phase }
454	        case .completed:
455	            answer = AgentServer.exportResult(
456	                settings: record.settings, burnInTimecode: record.burnInTimecode,
457	                path: record.destination.path, bytes: record.bytes, loudness: record.loudness,
458	                graphicWarnings: record.graphicWarnings, cursorWarnings: record.cursorWarnings)
459	        case .failed, .cancelled:
460	            answer["reason"] = record.message ?? ""
461	        case .waiting:
462	            // The memory hold's sentence, present only while held (spec §11 CX-18).
463	            if let held = record.message { answer["waiting"] = held }
464	        }
465	        if record.state == .waiting || record.state == .running,
466	            let seconds = ExportEncoderCosts.estimatedSeconds(for: record.settings)
467	        {
468	            answer["estimated_seconds"] = Int(seconds.rounded())
469	        }
470	        answer["export_id"] = id
471	        answer["status"] = AgentServer.exportStatusWord(record.state)
472	        answer["path"] = record.destination.path
473	        answer["elapsed"] = ((end - record.started) * 1000).rounded() / 1000
474	        return answer
475	    }
476	
477	    /// Copies every unfinished tracked job from the queue.
478	    private func refresh() {
479	        let queue = ExportQueueController.shared
480	        for (id, record) in records where record.finished == nil {
481	            guard let job = queue.job(id) else { continue }
482	            var updated = record
483	            updated.copy(job)
484	            records[id] = updated
485	        }
486	    }
487	}

490	/// What a finished export's answer carries: the resolved settings and the
491	/// facts about the file that was written, read off the queue's job once it
492	/// has finished — `export_status`'s `done` answer
493	/// (`AgentServer+ExportStatus.swift`), which since spec §11 #326 is what
494	/// `export` itself answered before it returned at once.
495	extension AgentServer {
496	
497	    /// The `done` answer's keys, exactly the ones `export` answered when it
498	    /// blocked to the file. `bytes` is the file's size as read at the finish.
499	    static func exportResult(
500	        settings: ExportSettings, burnInTimecode: Bool, path: String, bytes: Int,
501	        loudness: ExportLoudness?, graphicWarnings: [ExportGraphicWarning],
502	        cursorWarnings: [ExportCursorWarning]
503	    ) -> [String: Any] {
504	        var result: [String: Any] = [
505	            "ok": true,
506	            "path": path,
507	            "bytes": bytes,
508	            "preset": settings.preset,
509	            "container": settings.container,
510	            "codec": settings.codec,
511	            "width": settings.width,
512	            "height": settings.height,
513	            "fps": [settings.fps.num, settings.fps.den],
514	            "start": settings.start,
515	            "duration": settings.duration,
516	            // Not one of the resolved settings — the core never saw it — but
517	            // it is a fact about the file that was written, and every other
518	            // key here is one too.
519	            //
520	            // What it establishes is exactly one link and not the chain: this
521	            // is `options.burnInTimecode`, the local decoded a few lines up,
522	            // so a caller reading it back knows the argument was READ rather
523	            // than dropped in argument reading — the failure `boolArg`'s
524	            // refusal covers from the other side. It does NOT say the writer
525	            // used it; only a pixel can say that, and
526	            // `tools/proof/phase7_proof.py` is where one does.
527	            "burn_in_timecode": burnInTimecode,
528	        ]
529	        // The picture an HLG project's file was written as (`hlg`, `pq` or
530	        // `sdr`); absent for every SDR project and audio row.
531	        if let color = settings.color {
532	            result["dynamic_range"] = color
533	        }
534	        // The speed the `av1` row was encoded at (spec §11 CX-12 (2)); absent elsewhere.
535	        if let speed = settings.encoderSpeed {
536	            result["encoder_speed"] = speed.rawValue
537	        }
538	        // The depth a WAV or AIFF was written at (spec §11 AU-29); absent elsewhere.
539	        if let bits = settings.audioBits {
540	            result["audio_bits"] = bits
541	        }
542	        // Each stem written beside the mix, in order (spec §11 AU-108); absent without.
543	        if !settings.stems.isEmpty {
544	            let mix = URL(fileURLWithPath: path)
545	            result["stems"] = settings.stems.map {
546	                [
547	                    "name": $0.name, "tracks": $0.tracks,
548	                    "path": ExportStemsPipeline.url(for: $0, mix: mix).path,
549	                ] as [String: Any]
550	            }
551	        }
552	        if let measured = loudnessResult(loudness) {
553	            result["loudness"] = measured
554	        }
555	        if let warned = graphicWarningsResult(graphicWarnings) {
556	            result["graphic_warnings"] = warned
557	        }
558	        if let warned = cursorWarningsResult(cursorWarnings) {
559	            result["cursor_warnings"] = warned
560	        }
561	        return result
562	    }
563	
564	    /// What the export's sound MEASURED, for the result — nil, and then the
565	    /// key is simply absent, wherever `Exporter` published no report: a
566	    /// format that holds no audio track at all (GIF and APNG), and a
567	    /// timeline with no sound in it, which is the case a caller actually
568	    /// meets. A missing `loudness` is therefore "there was nothing to
569	    /// measure", never "the measurement was skipped".
570	    ///
571	    /// This is `detect_silence`'s posture applied to the writer: the numbers
572	    /// are read back off the file's own mix rather than repeated from the
573	    /// request, so a caller can check that a −14 LUFS export actually landed
574	    /// at −14, which is what makes phase 5's ±0.5 LU claim a claim anyone can
575	    /// test over MCP. `target` is what was ASKED for and is absent when
576	    /// nothing was — every export measures itself and reports, normalised or
577	    /// not.
578	    ///
579	    /// It is read off the queue's job (`ExportQueueController.Job.loudness`),
580	    /// which `finished` copies from the `Exporter` before dropping it:
581	    /// `Exporter.finish` publishes the report before it calls back, so every
582	    /// consumer (this, the queue's row and the progress sheet) reads it after
583	    /// the completion has fired.
584	    ///
585	    /// Every level goes through `jsonLevel`: a silent programme measures
586	    /// −∞ dBTP, and `JSONSerialization` throws on an infinity — which would
587	    /// report a successful export as a failed tool call.
588	    static func loudnessResult(_ report: ExportLoudness?) -> [String: Any]? {
589	        guard let report = report else { return nil }
590	        var measured: [String: Any] = [
591	            // The same sentence the progress sheet's last line shows, so the
592	            // two consumers of one measurement cannot describe it differently.
593	            "summary": report.summary,
594	            "true_peak_dbtp": jsonLevel(report.truePeakDBTP),
595	            // The shifted sample peak, never above the true peak the master
596	            // held (spec §11 AU-28).
597	            "sample_peak_dbfs": jsonLevel(
598	                min(report.measured.samplePeakDBFS + report.gainDB, report.truePeakDBTP)),
599	            "gain_db": report.gainDB,
600	            "ceiling_dbtp": jsonLevel(report.ceiling),
601	            "limited_db": report.limitedDB,
602	            "capped_by_gain": report.cappedByGain,
603	        ]
604	        // Absent rather than null, and for a reason worth the line: a
605	        // programme shorter than one 400 ms gating block, or one whose every
606	        // block fell under the standard's absolute gate, HAS no integrated
607	        // loudness. `summary` says so in words.
608	        if let integrated = report.integratedLUFS, integrated.isFinite {
609	            measured["integrated_lufs"] = integrated
610	        }
611	        if let target = report.target {
612	            measured["target_lufs"] = target
613	        }
614	        return measured
615	    }
616	
617	    /// Each distinct warning the export's graphics gave while the file was
618	    /// drawn (G-24 (c)), `[{name, frame, message}]` — `frame` the graphic's
619	    /// own, null when it has none — or nil, and then the key is absent,
620	    /// when there was none. Read off the queue's job after the completion,
621	    /// as `loudnessResult` is: `Exporter.finish` publishes it before the
622	    /// unpin. A failed export answers as it did.
623	    static func graphicWarningsResult(_ warnings: [ExportGraphicWarning]) -> [[String: Any]]? {
624	        guard !warnings.isEmpty else { return nil }
625	        return warnings.map {
626	            ["name": $0.name, "frame": $0.frame ?? NSNull(), "message": $0.message] as [String: Any]
627	        }
628	    }
629	
630	    /// Each media whose cursor file the export could not draw (spec §11
631	    /// CU-37 (c)), `[{media, path, message}]`, or nil, and then the key is
632	    /// absent, when there was none — `graphicWarningsResult`'s shape (G-24 (c)).
633	    static func cursorWarningsResult(_ warnings: [ExportCursorWarning]) -> [[String: Any]]? {
634	        guard !warnings.isEmpty else { return nil }
635	        return warnings.map {
636	            ["media": $0.media, "path": $0.path, "message": $0.message] as [String: Any]
637	        }
638	    }
639	}

| --- | --- | --- |
| Length | The module's `meta.durationInFrames` at the project's rate, else 5 seconds | At least one frame |
| Width and height | The module's `meta` size, else the canvas | 1 to 8192 pixels each |
| Properties | The schema's defaults | At most 64 |

Each property is checked against the module's schema when the clip is placed. A key the schema lacks, a value of the wrong type, a number out of range or an option that isn't listed is refused by its name. Colours are stored as lowercase hex.

Frame Job won't place the clip when:

- The module isn't in the folder. The refusal says what the folder holds.
- The module doesn't compile. The refusal gives its first error.
- A `meta` value it would use isn't a whole number in range. The refusal names the key.
- The canvas is wider or taller than 8192 pixels and no size was given. The refusal names the canvas.

## Change a clip

`set_graphic` changes what one or more graphic clips are drawn from: another module, the size, the graphic's own length or the properties. It's the same as editing **Properties**, **Size** and **Timeline** in the [Graphic sub-tab](/graphics/graphic-tab/).

- **Properties** merge key by key, and a clip stores at most 64. Clearing a property removes it. A property that an action on the clip animates is set to the module's default instead, so the animation keeps its start.
- **Length** snaps to a frame and is at least one frame. Clearing it is **Follow Clip**. See [Graphic size and timing](/graphics/size-and-timing/).
- **In** can't be set. The trims and splits own it.

These are the clip's base values. To animate one, add an action and set its end.

Clips drawn by two different modules can't take a property change together, and a clip that isn't a graphic is an error. A call that changes nothing makes no undo step, and that includes re-sending a colour in another spelling.

## Read a module or the folder

`get_graphic` with a name reads one module: its source, revision, path, whether it compiles, its `meta`, `schema` and problems, the clips it draws, and its kept versions, newest first. This is what the **Source** section shows a person.

With no name it reads the folder:

- The folder's path, given even before the folder exists. The first write creates it.
- Every module with its revision, whether it compiles and the clips it draws.
- The font families and pictures the project's graphics can use.
- Anything the folder's scan skipped or couldn't watch, in its own sentences.
- Every name with kept versions, deleted modules included.

## File tools

An agent can also edit the graphics folder with its own file tools, and Frame Job sees the change within a moment.

| What | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Modules | `graphics/<name>.js` |
| Fonts | `graphics/fonts/`, as `.ttf` or `.otf` |
| Pictures | `graphics/assets/` |

`history/`, `API.md` and `API.d.ts` are Frame Job's own, so leave them alone. `history/` holds the kept versions, and `API.md` and `API.d.ts` are the reference and its types.

In a project that hasn't been saved, the folder is a temporary one. It moves when the project is saved, so ask `get_graphic` for the path again afterwards.

See [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/) for how changes are picked up and how many files are watched.

## Undo rules

The files in `graphics/` live beside the project, not in its undo history. Changes to the clips on the timeline are ordinary undo steps.

| Action | Undo step? | Marks the project edited? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `write_graphic`, `restore_graphic`, `delete_graphic` | No | No |
| `import_graphic_font`, `import_graphic_asset` | No | No |
| `add_graphic_clip`, `insert_graphic`, `set_graphic` | Yes | Yes |
| `rename_graphic` | Yes, for the clips that follow the new name, as one step | Only through the clips |

Undoing a rename moves the file back along with the clips, and redo moves it forward again. `import_graphic` can't be undone either, and `export_graphic` edits nothing, so it has no undo step.

Because a file write can't be undone, Frame Job keeps the last 10 texts each module replaced, and `restore_graphic` brings one back. A deleted module's text is kept the same way. See [Rename, delete and restore graphics](/graphics/manage-graphics/).

## Graphics in render frame

`render_frame` shows a frame of the timeline as an export would draw it. When a graphic in that frame failed or warned, the answer has a sentence naming the graphic, its frame and the problem. A graphic that failed draws its error card in the picture. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/).

## The Assistant

The [Assistant tab](/assistant/what-it-can-do/) uses these same tools, so you can ask it in the inspector to write, change, place, render, rename, delete, restore, export and import graphics. It needs your [Anthropic key](/assistant/set-up/).

It asks before `export_graphic`, because that writes a package where the model chose and replaces any file already there. Nothing is written until you choose **Allow**. Importing a package doesn't ask, because it only writes inside the project's `graphics/`.
