---
title: "Tools: graphics"
description: "The agent tools that read the graphics API, write and check a module, list and insert graphics, and place and change graphic clips."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

These tools let an agent write a motion graphic, look at it without placing it, and put it on the timeline. [Graphics with an agent](/graphics/agents-and-graphics/) tells that story from the top. This page is the reference for each tool.

<AtAGlance
  tools={['graphic_reference', 'write_graphic', 'get_graphic', 'render_graphic', 'list_graphics', 'insert_graphic', 'add_graphic_clip', 'set_graphic']}
  needs="A client connected over MCP, or the Assistant tab."
/>

A graphic's code is a **module**, the file `graphics/<name>.js` inside the project, and `name` in these tools is that file's name without `.js`. Fonts, pictures, renames, deletes and packages are on [Tools: graphic fonts, pictures and packages](/mcp/tools-graphic-files/).

Every tool here also takes `project`, the path of an open project. Without it the call goes to the frontmost project. See [How tool calls behave](/mcp/tool-calls/). Times are in ticks, 600,000 a second, and are rounded to the project's frame grid. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/).

## Write, place, change and check

A graphic made by an agent usually goes through these steps.

<Steps>

1. Read the API once with [`graphic_reference`](#graphic_reference).

2. Write the module with [`write_graphic`](#write_graphic). The answer is the compile of that exact text. If it failed, fix the source and write it again.

3. Look at it with [`render_graphic`](#render_graphic), which draws frames with no clip on the timeline.

4. Place it with [`add_graphic_clip`](#add_graphic_clip), giving the track, the time and any values it should draw with. [`insert_graphic`](#insert_graphic) places a graphic at the playhead instead, as the Insert Graphic sheet does.

5. Change it with [`set_graphic`](#set_graphic). To animate a property, add an action with `add_action` and say what the property ends at with `set_action_end`. See [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/).

6. Check a frame of the finished timeline with [`render_frame`](/mcp/tools-render-and-export/#render_frame).

</Steps>

## `graphic_reference`

Answers the whole graphics API as Markdown, for a model to read once before it writes a graphic. It covers a module's shape, `ctx`, the schema's types, the standard library, fonts, the sandbox, the limits and worked examples.

It's the same file as **Help ▸ Graphics Reference**. See [The module API](/graphics/module-api/).

It takes no argument of its own, and it's the one tool on this page that needs no project open. A `project`, when given, must still name an open one.

## `write_graphic`

Writes a module's JavaScript into the project, compiles it and answers the compile of that text. The folder `graphics/` is made if it isn't there yet. A person does the same by saving the file in an editor. See [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | Yes | The module's name: lowercase letters, digits and `-`, starting with a letter or a digit, at most 63 characters. |
| `source` | string | Yes | The whole module's JavaScript. It exports `render`, and optionally `meta` and `schema`. |

It answers:

| Key | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `name`, `path`, `revision` | The module, its file, and the SHA-256 of its text. |
| `ok` | Whether the text compiled. |
| `meta`, `schema` | What the module declares. Both are empty when `ok` is false. |
| `diagnostics` | A list of `{level, message, line, column, frame}`. With `ok` false, they say where it went wrong. With `ok` true, they're the module's top-level warnings, such as `asset()` used outside `render`. |
| `clips` | The ids of the clips drawn by this module. They redraw with the new text at once. |
| `kept` | The module's kept earlier texts, newest first. |

A module that doesn't compile isn't an error. The call succeeds with `ok` false, and the file stays in the folder as written, so fix the source and write it again. The call itself fails only for a name that isn't a module name, or a file that can't be written.

A write can't be undone and doesn't mark the project edited, but the text it replaced is kept, up to the last 10 for each module. [`restore_graphic`](/mcp/tools-graphic-files/#restore_graphic) brings one back.

## `get_graphic`

Reads one module, or the whole graphics folder. The module's half is what the [**Source** section](/graphics/graphic-tab/#source) of the Graphic sub-tab shows a person.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | No | The module to read. Leave it out to read the folder. |

With `name`, it answers `name`, `source`, `path`, `revision`, `ok`, `meta`, `schema`, `diagnostics`, `clips` and `kept`, with the same meanings as [`write_graphic`](#write_graphic). A name the folder doesn't hold is refused, and the sentence lists what it does hold.

Without `name`, it answers:

| Key | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `folder` | The folder's full path. It's given even before the folder exists. |
| `folder_exists` | False until the first write makes the folder. |
| `modules` | Every module, as `{name, revision, ok, clips}`. |
| `families` | The font families the project's graphics can draw with. |
| `assets` | The pictures in `graphics/assets/`. |
| `warnings` | What the folder's scan skipped or couldn't watch, in sentences. |
| `history` | `{name, kept}` for every name with kept texts, deleted modules included. |

A module saved a moment ago from outside can read `ok` false with one diagnostic saying the app hasn't compiled it yet. Call again.

## `render_graphic`

Draws a module without a clip, to look at it before placing it. There's no control for this in the app, because a person looks at the preview instead.

### Render graphic options

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | Yes | The module to draw. |
| `frames` | array of integers | No | The frames to draw, 1 to 16 of them, in the order given. Not with `frame`. |
| `frame` | integer | No | One frame to draw, 0 or more. Not with `frames`. With neither, frame 0 is drawn. |
| `props` | object | No | The values to draw with, keyed by the schema's names. A key left out draws with the schema's default. |
| `width` | integer | No | The width to draw at, 1 to 8192 pixels. Default: `meta.width`, else the canvas. |
| `height` | integer | No | The height to draw at, 1 to 8192 pixels. Default: `meta.height`, else the canvas. |
| `format` | string | No | `png` (the default) for a contact sheet, or `svg` for one frame's text. |
| `max_width` | integer | No | The widest the sheet may be, 64 to 8192 pixels. The default is 2048. 8192 keeps a 1920-wide graphic's two cells at full size. |
| `background` | string | No | What the sheet is painted on: `transparent` (the default), `checker`, or a hex colour as `#rgb`, `#rrggbb` or `#rrggbbaa`, in either case. |
| `path` | string | No | Where to write the sheet. It's always a `.png`, and its folder must exist. Leave it out for a temporary file. |

`max_width`, `background` and `path` belong to the sheet, and `svg` won't take them.

Each frame is drawn as a clip would draw it. The frame rate is the canvas's, `durationInFrames` is the module's `meta` value or else 5 seconds, and a frame at or past that length is still drawn, with `progress` at 1, as a longer clip draws it.

### The contact sheet

The `png` format answers an image the model can see, a text block, and a file on disk. The frames sit on a near-square grid, top left first, and each frame's number is printed in a dark strip under its cell. Sixteen frames make a 4 by 4 grid.

- Only the cells scale down to fit `max_width`, never the 8-pixel gaps or the 24-pixel labels. Cells are never scaled up, and the sheet is never more than 8192 pixels tall.
- `checker` paints 16-pixel grey squares, which shows up a graphic's transparent areas.
- A frame that fails draws its error card in its cell. The sheet still comes back, and the text adds a sentence with the error and where it is. A frame that only warned adds a sentence too.
- The text says the frames, each cell's size and scale, the grid, the sheet's size and the background, and ends "Written to `<path>`."

A sheet draws at most 134,217,728 pixels of frames, counted as frames × width × height. That's two frames at 8192 × 8192, or sixteen at 3840 × 2160. Past that the call is refused before any frame is drawn, so ask for fewer frames or a smaller size.

### One frame as SVG

With `format: "svg"`, it answers `name`, `frame`, `ok`, `svg` (the frame's SVG text), `diagnostics`, and `ctx`, the values the frame was drawn with: `fps`, `time`, `durationInFrames`, `progress`, `width`, `height` and `canvas`.

It draws one frame and writes no file. A frame that fails isn't an error here either: `ok` is false, `svg` is null and `diagnostics` say why.

### When it refuses

`render_graphic` won't run when:

- The module isn't in the folder, or doesn't compile. The sentence lists what the folder holds, or gives the first error.
- Both `frame` and `frames` are given, or `frames` doesn't hold 1 to 16 whole numbers of 0 or more.
- `format` is `svg` with more than one frame, or with `path`, `background` or `max_width`.
- `max_width`, `width`, `height` or `background` is out of range, or the folder of `path` doesn't exist.
- A `meta` value it would use isn't a whole number in range. The sentence names the key.

## `list_graphics`

Lists the graphics **Insert ▸ Graphic…** offers, in the sheet's order. See [Insert a graphic](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/).

It takes no argument of its own. It answers `categories`, a list of `{name, graphics}`, and each graphic is:

| Key | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | What [`insert_graphic`](#insert_graphic) takes. |
| `title` | The module's `meta.name`, else its name made into a title. Two **This Project** graphics with one title show as "title — name". |
| `description` | The module's `meta.description`, or null. |
| `category` | The module's own category. |
| `from` | `template` or `project`, which is what `insert_graphic` takes as `from`. |
| `ok` | False for a module that doesn't compile. It's still listed. |

**This Project** comes first when the project's `graphics/` holds a module, and lists every module there, whatever its own category. The bundled templates follow by category, A to Z, each module's `meta.category` or else **Other**, which is always last. Within a category, graphics sort by title.

## `insert_graphic`

Places a graphic at the playhead, as the **Insert** button in **Insert ▸ Graphic…** does. See [Insert a graphic](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | Yes | The graphic's name as `list_graphics` gives it. |
| `from` | string | Yes | `template` for one of the bundled templates, `project` for a module already in the project's `graphics/`. |

The clip goes on the front track when it fits there, otherwise on a new track above everything, at the module's `meta` length and size. It's one undo step, **Insert Graphic**. With a nest open, it lands inside the nest.

A template is first copied into `graphics/` under a free name such as `lower-third` or `lower-third-2`. That copy can't be undone, so undoing the insert takes the clip away and leaves the module. A project module is placed as it is, with no copy.

It answers as an edit does, as described in [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/), and `name` says which module the clip is drawn by.

It won't place anything when:

- `name` isn't a template or a module of the project. The sentence lists what there is.
- The module doesn't compile. It gives the first error, and a template's copy stays in `graphics/`.
- A `meta` value it would use isn't a whole number in range.

## `add_graphic_clip`

Places a clip drawn by a module already in `graphics/`, on a track and at a time you choose. Use it when you need more say than `insert_graphic` gives. **Insert ▸ Graphic…** is a template's write followed by this. See [Place a clip](/graphics/agents-and-graphics/#place-a-clip).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `track` | integer | Yes | The track's id. `get_project` lists them. |
| `at` | integer | Yes | The start, in ticks. |
| `name` | string | Yes | The module. |
| `duration` | integer | No | The length, in ticks, at least one frame. Default: the module's `meta.durationInFrames` at the canvas's rate, else 5 seconds. |
| `width` | integer | No | The width the module draws at, 1 to 8192 pixels. Default: `meta.width`, else the canvas. |
| `height` | integer | No | The height the module draws at, 1 to 8192 pixels. Default: `meta.height`, else the canvas. |
| `props` | object | No | The values to draw with, keyed by the schema's names, at most 64. A key left out draws with the schema's default. |
| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to add the clip inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |

Like a shape, the clip has no source of its own. Use [`set_graphic`](#set_graphic) to change what it's drawn from, and `set_video` to place it in the picture.

Each key of `props` is checked against the module's schema as the file reads now. A key the schema lacks, a wrong type or a value out of range is refused by its dotted path. A colour is stored as lowercase hex, and a null is dropped.

It answers as an edit does, with the new clip in `new_clips`, and it's one undo step, **Add Graphic**.

It won't place the clip when:

- The module isn't in the folder, or doesn't compile. The sentence lists what the folder holds, or gives the first error.
- A `meta` value it would use isn't a whole number in range.
- The canvas is wider or taller than 8192 pixels and no size was given.
- The clip would overlap another one on the track, as for any clip.

## `set_graphic`

Changes what graphic clips are drawn from: the module, the size, the graphic's own length and its properties. It's the same as editing **Properties**, **Size** and **Timeline** in the [Graphic sub-tab](/graphics/graphic-tab/). See [Graphic properties](/graphics/properties/) and [Graphic size and timing](/graphics/size-and-timing/).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clip ids, at least one. |
| `patch` | object | Yes | The keys to change, below. |
| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside that nest. |

| Patch key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | Draws the clips from another module, which must be in the folder and compile. |
| `width`, `height` | The size the module draws at, 1 to 8192 pixels. |
| `length` | The graphic's own timeline, in ticks. It snaps to a frame and is at least one frame. Null ends it with the clip, which is **Follow Clip**. |
| `props` | The base values, merged key by key, at most 64 on a clip. A null removes its key. |

A null for a property that an action on the clip animates doesn't remove it. It sets the schema's default, so the animation keeps its start. To animate a property, use `add_action` and then `set_action_end`.

A patch with `props` or `name` is checked against a schema: the one of the module the patch names, otherwise the one module every clip is drawn by.

It answers as an edit does, and it's one undo step, **Graphic Properties**. A patch that changes nothing makes no undo step, and that includes a colour re-sent in another spelling.

It won't run when:

- One of the clips isn't a graphic. Nothing changes on the others either.
- `props` is sent to clips drawn by two different modules. Set them one module at a time.
- The patch has `in`, which the trims and splits own, or any other key it doesn't know.
- A value fails its check. The sentence gives its dotted path.

## Editing the folder with your own file tools

An agent can also edit the graphics folder directly, and Frame Job sees a change within a moment. Ask `get_graphic` with no `name` for the folder's path.

| What | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Modules | `<name>.js` |
| Fonts | `fonts/`, as `.ttf` or `.otf` |
| Pictures | `assets/` |

`history/`, `API.md` and `API.d.ts` are Frame Job's own, so leave them alone. `history/` holds the kept texts that `restore_graphic` reads, and `API.md` and `API.d.ts` are the reference.

A module's text is kept when Frame Job sees it replaced while the project is open, and that includes a save from an outside editor. See [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/) for how changes are picked up.

## Related

- [Graphics with an agent](/graphics/agents-and-graphics/)
- [Write a graphic module](/graphics/write-a-module/)
- [Tools: graphic fonts, pictures and packages](/mcp/tools-graphic-files/)
- [Patches](/mcp/patches/)

---
title: "Tools: graphic fonts, pictures and packages"
description: "The agent tools that add fonts and pictures to a project's graphics, rename, delete and restore modules, and export and import .fjgraphic packages."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

These tools look after the files around a graphic: the fonts and pictures it draws with, the module files themselves, and the `.fjgraphic` packages that carry a graphic from one project to another.

<AtAGlance
  tools={['import_graphic_font', 'import_graphic_asset', 'delete_graphic', 'rename_graphic', 'restore_graphic', 'export_graphic', 'import_graphic']}
  needs="A client connected over MCP, or the Assistant tab."
/>

Writing a module and placing it on the timeline are on [Tools: graphics](/mcp/tools-graphics/).

Every tool here also takes `project`, the path of an open project. Without it the call goes to the frontmost project. See [How tool calls behave](/mcp/tool-calls/). None of them takes `scope`.

## What can and cannot be undone

The files in `graphics/` live beside the project, not in its undo history. A change to the clips on the timeline is an ordinary undo step.

| Tool | Undo step? | Marks the project edited? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `write_graphic`, `restore_graphic`, `delete_graphic` | No | No |
| `import_graphic_font`, `import_graphic_asset`, `import_graphic` | No | No |
| `add_graphic_clip`, `insert_graphic`, `set_graphic` | Yes | Yes |
| `rename_graphic` | Yes, as one step, for the clips that follow the new name | Only through those clips |
| `export_graphic` | No, it edits nothing | No |

Because a file write can't be undone, Frame Job keeps the last 10 texts of each module. A text is kept whenever Frame Job sees a module replaced while the project is open, whether by `write_graphic`, a save from an outside editor or a restore, and when `delete_graphic` removes one. [`restore_graphic`](#restore_graphic) brings one back. `insert_graphic`'s copy of a template can't be undone either, even though the clip it places can.

Fonts and pictures aren't kept this way. Importing over a file of the same name replaces it for good.

## Fonts and pictures together

A module draws with two kinds of file besides its code. [`import_graphic_font`](#import_graphic_font) adds a font and [`import_graphic_asset`](#import_graphic_asset) adds a picture.

Both take the `path` of a file on this Mac, with `~` expanded, and copy it into the project. The folders are made if they aren't there. Graphics can use the file as soon as the call answers, and a file already at that name is replaced. A `path` that names no file is refused.

Each answer tells the agent what to write in the module: the exact family names for a font, the name for `asset()` for a picture. See [Fonts and pictures in graphics](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/).

## `import_graphic_font`

Copies a `.ttf` or `.otf` file into the project's `graphics/fonts/` and answers the family names to use. It mirrors **File ▸ Add Font to Graphics…**. See [Add a font](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/#add-a-font).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | Yes | The font file to copy. |

It answers:

| Key | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `families` | The family names read from this file. These are the exact strings a `font-family` must say, and they can differ from what other apps show. |
| `library_families` | Every family the project's graphics can now draw with. |
| `path`, `name` | Where the copy landed, and the file's name. |
| `replaced` | True when a file of the same name was replaced. |

It won't copy a file that isn't `.ttf` or `.otf`, one it can't read, or one that loads no typeface. The last gives the graphics engine's own reason.

## `import_graphic_asset`

Copies a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, SVG or SVGZ picture into the project's `graphics/assets/`, where a module draws it with `<image href="${asset(name)}">`. It mirrors **File ▸ Add Image to Graphics…**. See [Add a picture](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/#add-a-picture).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | Yes | The picture to copy. |
| `name` | string | No | The name to file it under, which is what `asset(name)` says. Its extension must be `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.gif`, `.webp`, `.svg` or `.svgz`. Default: the file's own name. |

It answers `name`, `path`, `replaced`, `bytes`, `assets` (every picture the folder now holds) and `renamed_from` when the name had to change.

`asset(name)` can't use a name that starts with `.` or `#`, holds any of `:`, `"`, `'`, `<`, `>` or `&` or a control character, or runs past 247 bytes. Frame Job files such a picture under a legal name instead. `name` says which, and `renamed_from` says what was asked. A renamed copy never replaces a file. It takes `-2`, `-3` and so on. See [Picture names](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/#picture-names).

It won't copy:

- A file whose name doesn't end in one of the six extensions.
- An empty file.
- Anything when `name` is empty or holds a `/`.

## `delete_graphic`

Deletes a module no clip draws, keeping its text so it can come back. It mirrors **File ▸ Delete Graphic…**. See [Delete Graphic](/graphics/manage-graphics/#delete-graphic).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | Yes | The module to delete. |

It answers `ok`, `name`, `revision` (the deleted text's), `kept` and a note. The kept text joins the module's others, `get_graphic` with no `name` lists it under `history`, and [`restore_graphic`](#restore_graphic) brings it back. Fonts and pictures are left alone.

It won't delete when:

- The folder doesn't hold the module. The sentence lists what it does hold.
- A clip is still drawn by it, on the timeline or inside a nest. The sentence names them, for example "clips 4 and 9 on the timeline and clip 12 in nest 7". Delete those clips, or point them at another module with `set_graphic`, first.
- Its text can't be kept. The file stays where it is.

## `rename_graphic`

Renames a module, and every clip drawn by it follows, on the timeline and inside every nest. It mirrors **File ▸ Rename Graphic…**. See [Rename Graphic](/graphics/manage-graphics/#rename-graphic).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | Yes | The module to rename. |
| `to` | string | Yes | The new name: lowercase letters, digits and `-`, starting with a letter or a digit, at most 63 characters. |

It answers `ok`, `name` (the new name), `renamed_from`, `clips` (the ids that followed), `revision`, `kept` and a note.

The clips' change is one undo step, **Rename Graphic**. Undo renames the file back with the clips, and redo moves both forward again. A module no clip draws makes no undo step, so to go back, rename it again.

The module's kept texts move with it. When `to` is a deleted module's name, with no file but kept texts, the two sets join under `to`. Past 10, the oldest texts, the deleted module's, are dropped for good.

It won't rename when:

- The folder doesn't hold the module.
- `to` isn't a module name.
- `graphics/<to>.js` already exists.
- A clip already names `to` with no file behind it, a clip left by a deleted module. Delete that clip or point it at another module first.
- A nest is open, because a rename reaches every clip in the project. `set_scope` with no arguments comes back out.

## `restore_graphic`

Writes a kept earlier text of a module back, compiles it and answers as [`write_graphic`](/mcp/tools-graphics/#write_graphic) does. It works for a module `delete_graphic` removed. It mirrors **File ▸ Restore Graphic Version…**, which always restores the newest. See [Restore Graphic Version](/graphics/manage-graphics/#restore-graphic-version).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | Yes | The module, present or deleted. |
| `revision` | string | No | The kept revision to put back, one of `kept` as `get_graphic` lists them. Default: the newest kept. |

It answers `name`, `path`, `revision`, `ok`, `meta`, `schema`, `diagnostics`, `clips`, then `restored`, the revision put back, and `kept`, what's kept now.

The text it replaced is kept in turn, so restoring twice returns you to where you were.

It won't restore when:

- The module has no kept text.
- `revision` isn't one of its kept revisions. The sentence lists them.
- The kept file was changed outside Frame Job, so it no longer holds that revision. Nothing is written, and the sentence lists the module's other kept revisions.

## `export_graphic`

Writes one graphic as a `.fjgraphic` package: a zip of a manifest, the module, and only the project fonts and pictures it was seen to use. It mirrors **Export…** in **Insert ▸ Graphic…**. See [Share a graphic](/graphics/share-a-graphic/).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | Yes | The graphic's name as `list_graphics` gives it. |
| `from` | string | Yes | `template` for a bundled template, `project` for a module in the project's `graphics/`. |
| `path` | string | Yes | Where to write it. `.fjgraphic` is added when the path lacks it, and its folder must exist. An existing file is replaced. |

To find out what a graphic uses, Frame Job draws it:

1. Every frame up to 900 with the default properties. A longer graphic gets 900 evenly spaced frames.
2. Then each `enum` option other than the default, and each boolean's opposite, over 30 frames each. It tries at most 32 of these.

It packs the project fonts and pictures the engine drew, measured, fell back to or resolved. A bundled font is never packed. String and asset properties are only tried at their defaults, so a picture chosen by another value of one won't be found. See [What a package packs](/graphics/share-a-graphic/#what-a-package-packs).

It answers:

| Key | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `path` | The file written. |
| `files` | The package's entries, `manifest.json` first. |
| `frames` | How many frames were drawn. |
| `failed_frames` | The frames that threw and were skipped. |

It writes nothing for an unknown name, a module that doesn't compile, or a folder that doesn't exist. It's no edit and no undo step.

## `import_graphic`

Copies a `.fjgraphic` package into the project's `graphics/`: its module, fonts and pictures, under the names the package gives. It does what opening a package from the Finder or **From File…** in **Insert ▸ Graphic…** does, but there's no sheet to confirm it. It places no clip. Use `insert_graphic` with `from: "project"` for that. See [Share a graphic](/graphics/share-a-graphic/).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | Yes | The `.fjgraphic` file to import. `~` is expanded. |

The package is checked first: a stored zip whose entries match its manifest by path, size and SHA-256, in a format this app reads, with each font loading and each picture under a name `asset(name)` can use. A package that fails is refused, in a sentence beginning "`<file>` cannot be imported:", and nothing is written. See [Package checks](/graphics/share-a-graphic/#package-checks).

Each file then goes in without replacing anything:

| If the name in the project | A module or font | A picture |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Is free | Is written | Is written |
| Holds the same bytes | Is reused | Is reused |
| Holds something else | Takes `-2`, `-3` and so on | Stops the whole import |

A picture can't take a new name, because the module reaches it by name. A name that differs only in case counts as taken. If a write fails part-way, what was written is removed.

It answers:

| Key | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | The module, as named in this project. |
| `renamed_from` | What the package called it, when the name changed. |
| `title` | The graphic's title. |
| `module` | `written` or `reused`. |
| `fonts` | A list of `{name, renamed_from, action}`, with `renamed_from` only when it changed. |
| `assets` | A list of `{name, action}`. |

It can't be undone.

## Related

- [Tools: graphics](/mcp/tools-graphics/)
- [Graphics with an agent](/graphics/agents-and-graphics/)
- [Rename, delete and restore graphics](/graphics/manage-graphics/)
- [Share a graphic](/graphics/share-a-graphic/)

<system-reminder>
Contents of /Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob/.claude/worktrees/help-docs/docs/site/CLAUDE.md:

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, Node is pinned by `.node-version`. `README.md` has the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

</system-reminder>

---
title: "Tools: rendering and export"
description: "The agent tools that render one frame of the timeline, start an export, follow it on the Export Queue and stop it."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

These tools turn the timeline into pictures and files. `render_frame` is how an agent sees what it has done, and `export`, `export_status` and `cancel_export` write the finished file.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['File ▸ Save Frame…', 'File ▸ Export…', 'Window ▸ Export Queue']}
  keys="⌘E"
  tools={['render_frame', 'export', 'export_status', 'cancel_export']}
  needs="A client connected over MCP, or the Assistant tab."
/>

Each tool has a heading here with its arguments. [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/) and [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/) walk through using them.

Every tool here also takes `project`, the path of an open project. Without it the call goes to the frontmost project. See [How tool calls behave](/mcp/tool-calls/). None of them takes `scope`.

## `render_frame`

Renders one frame of the finished timeline as a picture the model can see and a file on disk. It goes through the same composition and compositor an export does, so it shows what the file will hold at that moment. Use it before and after every edit. It's the same writer as **File ▸ Save Frame…**, so a PNG written here and one saved from the menu are byte-identical. See [Save Frame](/export/save-frame/).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `t` | integer | No | The moment to render, in ticks, rounded to the frame grid. Default: the playhead. |
| `path` | string | No | Where to write the file. The folder must exist. Default: a temporary file. |
| `format` | string | No | `png`, `jpeg` or `heic`. Default: the path's own extension when it's one of those, else `png`. An explicit format wins, and the path's extension is replaced, so `shot.jpg` with `png` writes `shot.png`. |
| `max_width` | integer | No | Caps the image's width, 16 to 8192 pixels, aspect kept and never scaled up. Default: the canvas's own size. |
| `burn_in_timecode` | boolean | No | Draws the project timecode over the picture, topmost. Default: false. See [Burn in timecode](/export/burn-in-timecode/). |
| `ungraded` | boolean | No | Draws as if no clip were graded, which is **View ▸ Show Ungraded**'s picture. Default: false. See [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/). |
| `sdr_version` | boolean | No | Draws an HDR project's SDR version, which is **View ▸ Show SDR Version**'s picture. An SDR project's frame doesn't change. Default: false. See [Show SDR Version](/hdr/show-sdr-version/). |
| `selection` | integer | No | An adjustment clip's id. Draws what its qualifier selects, which is **View ▸ Show Selection**'s picture: grey, white fully graded and black untouched, with every layer in front of the clip left out. Black where the clip isn't on the frame. See [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/). |
| `waveform` | boolean | No | Also measures the frame's luma waveform. Default: false. |
| `parade` | boolean | No | Also measures the frame's RGB parade. Default: false. |
| `vectorscope` | boolean | No | Also measures the frame's vectorscope. Default: false. |
| `vectorscope_zoom` | integer | No | The vectorscope's zoom: 1, 2 or 4. Needs `vectorscope: true`. Default: 1. |
| `histogram` | boolean | No | Also measures the frame's histogram. Default: false. |

The view switches themselves never reach this tool, so an agent asks for each picture here, whatever a person has switched on.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `export_id` | integer | Yes | The `export_id` that `export` answered, 1 or more. |

| --- | --- |

| `failed`, `cancelled` | `reason`, the queue row's sentence. |

| --- | --- |
| `ok`, `bytes` | True, and the file's size. |
| `preset`, `container`, `codec`, `width`, `height`, `fps`, `start`, `duration` | The settings used. `fps` is `[num, den]`, and the width and height are the file's. |
| `burn_in_timecode` | Whether the burn-in was asked for. |
| `dynamic_range` | In an HDR project, the picture written. |
| `encoder_speed` | On `av1` and `av1_webm`. |
| `audio_bits` | On `audio_wav` and `audio_aiff`. |

Stops an export, as **Cancel** in its Export Queue row does. See [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `export_id` | integer | Yes | The `export_id` that `export` answered, 1 or more. |

A queued export is cancelled before it starts. A running one stops and its half-written file is removed, though the answer may still read `running` until the writer has stopped, when `export_status` reads `cancelled`. A finished export is left alone.

It answers as `export_status` does, and it refuses an id `export` didn't answer since launch.

`integrated_lufs` is absent for a programme too short or too quiet to have one, and `summary` says so in words. `limited_db` says how far the limiter turned the hottest peak down, and `capped_by_gain` is true when the +40 dB gain cap decided the gain.

Only ids `export` answered since Frame Job launched are known. Anything else is refused, and that includes a job a person put on the queue. A finished job's answer outlives its queue row, so it still reads after **Remove** or **Clear Finished**.

## `cancel_export`

Stops an export, as **Cancel** in its Export Queue row does. See [The Export Queue](/export/export-queue/).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `export_id` | integer | Yes | The `export_id` that `export` answered, 1 or more. |

A queued export is cancelled before it starts. A running one stops and its half-written file is removed, though the answer may still read `running` until the writer has stopped, when `export_status` reads `cancelled`. A finished export is left alone.

It answers as `export_status` does, and it refuses an id `export` didn't answer since launch.

- [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/)
- [Export: start, then poll](/mcp/export/)
- [What an export includes](/export/what-an-export-includes/)
- [Transparent exports](/export/transparency/)

---
title: "Tools: recording and screencasts"
description: "The agent tools that record the screen, a camera or the microphone, read and attach cursor files, and add zooms, shortcut overlays and faster typing to a screencast."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

These tools make a recording and then polish it as a screencast. `record_screen` records. The rest read the cursor file Frame Job writes beside a screen recording, and use what it holds to zoom on clicks, show shortcuts and speed through typing.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['File ▸ New Recording…', 'Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…', 'Clip ▸ Add Shortcut Overlays', 'Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…']}
  where="Media tab ▸ Cursor"
  tools={['record_screen', 'set_media_cursor', 'get_cursor_events', 'auto_zoom', 'add_shortcut_overlays', 'speed_up_typing']}
  needs="Recording needs its system grants, which only a person can give. The rest runs on your Mac with no key."
/>

Every tool here also takes `project`, the path of an open project. Without it the call goes to the frontmost project. See [How tool calls behave](/mcp/tool-calls/). Times are in ticks, 600,000 a second. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/).

## The tools that work from a cursor file

`auto_zoom`, `add_shortcut_overlays` and `speed_up_typing` share these rules:

- Each takes exactly one of `clip` and `clips`.
- `from` and `to` are in the time of the timeline or nest that's open, and `to` must be after `from`. The menu commands can't limit themselves this way.
- None takes `scope`. Each acts in whatever `set_scope` has open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).
- None remembers the settings a person last used in a sheet. They start from the defaults below.
- With nothing to do, each answers `ok` with a `note` and makes no undo step.

Each one won't run when a clip isn't a media clip, its media has no cursor file or the file is missing, or it plays reversed. If the project changes while the cursor files are read, the call changes nothing and says to call again.

## `record_screen`

Records for a set number of seconds and lands the result as ordinary media, as **File ▸ New Recording…** does without the panel. It records a display or a window, the microphone alone, or a camera alone, and it can record a camera beside the screen. [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/) has the whole story. See also [The recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `seconds` | number | Yes | How long to record, 1 to 600. |
| `source` | string | No | `screen` (the default), `voice_over` for the default microphone alone, or `camera` for a camera alone. |
| `display` | integer | No | Which display, with 0 the main one. Default: 0. Not with `window`. |
| `window` | integer | No | A window's id, to record that window on its own at its own size. Not with `display`. |
| `size` | string | No | `nominal` (the default) records the display's point size, and `best` its pixel size. |
| `rate` | integer | No | The capture's frame rate, 30 or 60. Default: 60. It's also the canvas rate of a new project the recording opens as. |
| `system_audio` | boolean | No | Captures what every application but Frame Job plays, as the movie's stereo 48 kHz track. Default: true. |
| `microphone` | boolean | No | Records the default microphone to a second file beside the movie. Default: false. |
| `show_clicks` | boolean | No | Shows each mouse click. With `cursor` `separate`, the clips land with click ripples. With `in_picture`, a circle goes into the movie. Default: false. |
| `cursor` | string | No | `separate` keeps the pointer out of the movie and Frame Job draws it, and `in_picture` burns it in. Default: `separate`. |
| `keys` | string | No | `off` (the default), or `shortcuts` to write each shortcut pressed and a time-only mark for every other key into the cursor file, never which key was typed. Needs the Input Monitoring grant. |
| `include_framejob_windows` | boolean | No | Puts Frame Job's own windows in a display recording. Default: false. |
| `camera` | string | No | With `source` `camera`, the camera to record alone. Default: the system's preferred camera, else the first built-in, else the first. With `source` `screen`, a camera to record beside the screen. Default: none. A device's unique id, or its name in any case. |
| `camera_format` | string | No | The format, such as `1920x1080@30`, or `WIDTHxHEIGHT` for that size's highest rate, or `best`. Default: `best`. |
| `camera_layout` | string | No | With a camera beside the screen, where it lands: `corner_square` (the default, bottom right), `corner_rounded`, `corner_circle`, `side_by_side` or `camera_full`. |
| `camera_cutout` | boolean | No | With a camera beside the screen, runs Remove Background on the camera clips as its own undo step. Default: false. |
| `enhance` | boolean | No | Runs `enhance_voice` on the microphone's clips once their sound is analysed, as its own undo step. Default: false. |
| `auto_zoom` | boolean | No | Runs [`auto_zoom`](#auto_zoom) on the screen clips as its own undo step. Default: false. |
| `shortcut_overlays` | boolean | No | Runs [`add_shortcut_overlays`](#add_shortcut_overlays) on the screen clips, after `auto_zoom`, as its own undo step. Needs `keys: "shortcuts"`. Default: false. |
| `speed_up_typing` | boolean | No | Runs [`speed_up_typing`](#speed_up_typing) on the screen clips, last, once their speech is detected, as its own undo step. Needs `keys: "shortcuts"`. Default: false. |
| `place` | boolean | No | Puts the clips on the timeline at the playhead, in one undo step with the media. `false` adds the media and no clip, except in a new project, whose first picture is the document. Default: true. |
| `path` | string | No | A folder to record into, made if it doesn't exist. Default: `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings`. It names the folder, never the file. |

Only some of these go together:

| With | Frame Job won't take |
| --- | --- |
| `source: "voice_over"` | `display`, `window`, `system_audio`, `show_clicks`, `size`, `include_framejob_windows`, `keys`, `cursor`, `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays`, `speed_up_typing`, any `camera` argument, or `microphone: false` |
| `source: "camera"` | `display`, `window`, `system_audio`, `show_clicks`, `size`, `include_framejob_windows`, `keys`, `cursor`, `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays`, `speed_up_typing`, `camera_layout`, `camera_cutout` or `rate` |
| `source: "screen"` with no `camera` | `camera_format`, `camera_layout` or `camera_cutout` |
| `place: false` | `enhance`, `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays`, `speed_up_typing`, `camera_layout` or `camera_cutout` |

`enhance` also needs `microphone: true` or a voice-over.

The call blocks for the whole recording, plus about a second to start and finish, and longer if the files are slow to close. It answers `path`, `media`, `clip`, `duration`, `width`, `height`, `fps`, `has_audio`, `audio_tracks`, `pauses`, `segments` with one entry for each file, `stopped_by` and `landed`, plus the microphone's and the camera's own keys when they're used, and a `note` when there's something to say. Each polish step adds its own answer under its name, or a sentence under `<name>_error`, such as `auto_zoom_error`.

A person at the Mac can pause, resume and stop an agent's recording from the [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/) or the **File** menu. A pause shortens what's recorded, because `seconds` is wall-clock time, and a stop ends it early and it still lands.

**It never asks for a grant.** The Screen Recording, Microphone, Camera and Input Monitoring grants must already be held, and a missing one is refused by name with the System Settings pane. The recorder panel is where a person gives them. See [Recording permissions](/recording/permissions/). Frame Job started from a shell runs under the terminal's grants, not the app's.

It checks in a fixed order: your own arguments first, then the camera and its format, then the grants, then the display or window. A locked console or sleeping displays are refused as that, by name. An unknown camera or format is refused naming what's there.

## `set_media_cursor`

Attaches, moves or removes a screen recording's cursor file, the `.fjcursor` Frame Job writes beside each recorded movie. It's **Locate…** and **Remove** in the Media tab's **Cursor** section. See [Cursor files](/recording/cursor-files/).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `media` | integer | Yes | The video media's id. |
| `cursor` | object | Yes | `{path, bookmark?, in_picture}`, the media's `cursor` as `get_project` shows it, or null to forget the file. The file itself stays on disk. |
| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to make the edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |

Give `path` in full, because `~` isn't expanded here. `in_picture` says whether the movie's picture already shows the pointer, and it must match the file.

It answers as an edit does, with `media` added, and it's one undo step, **Locate Cursor File** or **Remove Cursor File**. **Consolidate Media** copies the file into the package beside its movie, and opening a moved package finds it there.

It won't attach the file when:

- `path` is empty.
- The file doesn't open as a cursor file.
- The file was made for a movie of a different size.
- `in_picture` isn't the file's own.
- The media isn't a video with a picture.

## `get_cursor_events`

Reads what a recording's cursor file holds: its clicks, scrolls, shortcuts, stretches of typing and, if asked, the pointer's path. It runs on your Mac, needs no key, edits nothing and makes no undo step. There's no menu for it. See [What a cursor file holds](/recording/cursor-files/#what-a-cursor-file-holds).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `media` | integer | One of these | The recording, read in the file's own source ticks. |
| `clip` | integer | One of these | A media clip of a recording, read in ticks from the clip's start, through its speed and ramps. |
| `from` | integer | No | Where to start, in ticks, in the answer's time. Default: 0. |
| `to` | integer | No | Where to stop, not included, in ticks. Must be after `from`. Default: the media's or the clip's duration. |
| `kinds` | array of strings | No | Any of `clicks`, `scrolls`, `shortcuts`, `typing` and `path`. Default: the first four. |
| `smoothing` | number | No | The path's smoothing, 0 to 1. Default: the clip's own **Smoothing** in its Cursor section, else 0, the raw path. |

It answers `ok`, `time` (`media` or `clip`), `from`, `to`, `count`, `media`, `clip` when given, `size` as `[w, h]`, `cursor_file`, `in_picture`, a `project` summary, and one key for each kind asked for:

| Key | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `clicks` | A list of `{t, button, down, count, x, y}`. `button` is 0 left, 1 right, 2 other. `down` is 1 for a press and 0 for a release. |
| `scrolls` | A list of `{t, x, y, dx, dy}`, each a single wheel event, with `dx` and `dy` in points. |
| `shortcuts` | A list of `{t, keys, code}`. |
| `typing` | A list of `{from, to, marks}`, each stretch that overlaps the window. |
| `path` | `{smoothing, t, x, y}`, sampled 10 times a second. |

`x` and `y` are the movie's own pixels from its top left.

**Zoom on a click.** With `clip`, each click and scroll also has `q`, as `[qx, qy]`: its position as an offset in source pixels from the centre of the clip's cropped picture. That's the frame `add_zoom_action`'s region takes, so a region around a click is `{x: qx, y: qy, w, h}`. See [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/).

**Long recordings.** Rows of every kind and path samples count together, and an answer holds at most 5,000. `next` is then the first time left out, so call again with `from: next`.

It won't read when:

- It doesn't get exactly one of `media` and `clip`.
- `kinds` is empty or names something else, or `smoothing` is outside 0 to 1.
- `to` isn't after `from`.
- The clip isn't a media clip, or it plays reversed. Ask with its media instead.
- The media has no cursor file, or the file is missing.

## `auto_zoom`

Plans screencast zooms from the clicks and typing in a recording's cursor file, and applies them as one undo step, **Auto Zoom**. It's **Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…**. See [Auto Zoom](/recording/auto-zoom/).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clip` | integer | One of these | A screen recording's media clip. |
| `clips` | array of integers | One of these | Media clips whose media have cursor files. |
| `zoom` | number | No | How far in, times the clip's own scale: 1.25 to 4. Default: 2. |
| `lead` | number | No | Arrive this many seconds before the click: 0.2 to 2. Default: 0.6. |
| `stay` | number | No | Stay this many seconds after the last activity: 0.5 to 10. Default: 2.5. |
| `follow` | boolean | No | Follows the pointer while zoomed. Default: true. |
| `typing` | boolean | No | Zooms on stretches of typing too. Default: true. |
| `replace` | boolean | No | Removes the clips' existing zooms first. Default: false. |
| `motion_blur` | number | No | The shutter given to each zoomed clip whose own `motion_blur` is 0, as a fraction of a frame: 0 to 1. Default: 0.5, a 180° shutter. 0 sets none. |
| `from` | integer | No | Plans only clicks and typing at or after this time, in ticks. With `replace`, removes only zooms that meet the `from` to `to` window. |
| `to` | integer | No | Plans only before this time, in ticks. |

Each zoom is an ordinary action, the shape `add_zoom_action` makes, so it can be edited like any other. A visit starts at a click, or at a stretch of typing aimed at the last click before it. It zooms in `lead` seconds before that and back out over 0.8 seconds, `stay` seconds after the last activity. [How a visit is planned](/recording/auto-zoom/#how-a-visit-is-planned) has the rest.

Halves of a split are planned as one, and nothing straddles a cut. See [Across a split](/recording/auto-zoom/#across-a-split). A planned zoom that meets an action already on the clip is dropped. `replace` removes only zooms, never any other action. A clip that already has a shutter keeps it.

It answers as an edit does, and adds:

| Key | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `visits` | How many visits were planned. |
| `added`, `replaced`, `dropped` | Zooms added, existing zooms removed, and planned zooms dropped because they met an action. |
| `closed_at_cut` | Visits closed at a cut, because the later half has an action of its own there. |
| `bases_set` | Later halves whose base was set by a zoom held across a cut. |
| `blurred` | How many clips were given `motion_blur`. |
| `actions` | A list of `{clip, at, duration, kind}`, with `at` in clip ticks and `kind` one of `in`, `pan`, `follow` or `back`. |

Besides [the shared rules](#the-tools-that-work-from-a-cursor-file), it won't run when a number is out of range, a clip has no picture, or a clip is placed smaller than the canvas. For that last one, nest the clip, open the nest with `set_scope` and call `auto_zoom` inside it.

## `add_shortcut_overlays`

Places one Keyboard keys graphic clip for each keyboard shortcut recorded, at the moment it was pressed, as one undo step, **Add Shortcut Overlays**. It's **Clip ▸ Add Shortcut Overlays**, which has no sheet, so an agent is the only way to choose these settings. See [Shortcut overlays](/recording/shortcut-overlays/).

Only shortcuts are recorded, never typed keys, and only when the recording was made with **Record shortcuts** or `keys: "shortcuts"`. See [Record shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clip` | integer | One of these | A screen recording's media clip. |
| `clips` | array of integers | One of these | Media clips whose media have cursor files. |
| `duration` | number | No | How long each overlay shows, in seconds: 0.5 to 10. Default: 1.5. |
| `position` | string | No | Where the keycaps sit: `bottom` (the default), `center` or `top`. |
| `theme` | string | No | The keycaps' look: `dark` (the default) or `light`. |
| `from` | integer | No | Places only shortcuts at or after this time, in ticks. |
| `to` | integer | No | Places only shortcuts before this time, in ticks. |

An overlay never lasts less than 10 frames for each keycap plus 25, the time the template needs to press its last key and exit. Overlays never overlap:

- The same shortcut pressed again before its overlay ends extends it, labelled ×2, ×3 and so on.
- A different shortcut pressed sooner ends the earlier overlay where it starts, once the earlier one has had its minimum. If that puts it more than 0.5 seconds after its press, it's dropped.

The clips go on the front-most track named **Shortcuts** when it's in front of every clip's track, unlocked, shown, not a matte and free over their span. Otherwise they go on a new **Shortcuts** track at the front. A module in `graphics/` whose text equals the bundled template is reused, and otherwise the template is copied in once, only when something is placed.

The overlays are ordinary graphic clips. See [Change an overlay](/recording/shortcut-overlays/#change-an-overlay).

It answers as an edit does, and adds:

| Key | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `added`, `merged`, `dropped` | Overlays placed, repeat presses folded into one, and presses left out. |
| `track`, `new_track` | The track used, and whether it's new. |
| `module`, `written` | The module drawn, and whether the template was copied in. |
| `overlays` | A list of `{at, duration, keys, label}`, with `at` in timeline ticks. |

Besides [the shared rules](#the-tools-that-work-from-a-cursor-file), it won't run with a `duration`, `position` or `theme` out of range.

## `speed_up_typing`

Plays the typing in screen recordings faster, keeping speech and shortcuts at normal speed, as one undo step, **Speed Up Typing**. It's **Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…**. See [Speed Up Typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clip` | integer | One of these | A screen recording's media clip. |
| `clips` | array of integers | One of these | Media clips whose media have cursor files. Halves of a split recording are joined. |
| `rate` | number | No | How much faster a stretch plays: 2 to 8. Default: 4. |
| `shortest` | number | No | The shortest stretch sped up, in seconds: 1 to 30. Default: 3. |
| `keep_pitch` | boolean | No | Keeps the sped sound's pitch. Default: true. |
| `from` | integer | No | Speeds only typing at or after this time, in ticks. |
| `to` | integer | No | Speeds only typing before this time, in ticks. |

A typing stretch is a run of at least 3 typed keys, each under 1 second apart. Taken out of each stretch are every span of speech, in any clip with sound under it on any track, and each recorded shortcut with its overlay, which is 1.5 seconds when it has no clip on a **Shortcuts** track. The pieces of all the clips join where they meet, and a piece shorter than `shortest` is left alone.

Each kept piece is sped by `retime_range` at `rate` on every unlocked track, keeping 0.3 seconds at normal speed at each end, so everything after it moves up in step. See [Tools: speed and time](/mcp/tools-speed/).

Speech detection runs on your Mac. A media with sound under a stretch that has no speech saved yet gets its spans in the same step.

It answers:

| Key | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `stretches`, `short` | Stretches found, and pieces left alone for being too short. |
| `ranges` | A list of `{from, to, sped_to}`, in timeline ticks before the edit. |
| `saved` | The time saved, in ticks. |
| `speech_saved` | The media whose speech was saved in this step. |
| `audio_left_out`, `audio_note` | Only when a clip with sound now plays past ×12, the ceiling for sound. Unlike the menu command, it doesn't ask. See [If a clip would go silent](/recording/speed-up-typing/#if-a-clip-would-go-silent). |

Besides [the shared rules](#the-tools-that-work-from-a-cursor-file), it won't run, and nothing changes, when:

- `rate` or `shortest` is out of range.
- `retime_range` would refuse any range, because of a locked track after it, a transition or a linked clip, for example. The sentence names it.
- Speech detection is still running. It doesn't wait, and it says to try again in a moment.

## Related

- [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/)
- [Cursor files](/recording/cursor-files/)
- [Polish when a recording lands](/recording/when-it-lands/)
- [Tools: speed and time](/mcp/tools-speed/)
